The Mark Twain Prize ceremony streamed on Netflix this week, with comic Whitney Cummings hosting the comedy awards show – but one of her jokes about Donald Trump didn’t make it into the final edit.

The comedian, 43, made an edgy quip – which appeared to reference the US president’s former friendship with the late child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein – during the ceremony at the John F Kennedy Center when it was filmed earlier this year. Trump vehemently denies any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein and has not been accused of criminal misconduct.

While the joke was reported at the time, it didn’t make it into Netflix’s streamed special of the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor on Tuesday (21 July), which honoured political commentator and TV presenter Bill Maher.

open image in gallery Cummings spoke about the edit on her podcast ( Youtube: Whitney Cummings )

Speaking on her Good for You podcast on Monday about the joke being axed, Cummings said that the bosses of the venue – which has Trump as its chairman – have been “amazing”.

“They don’t want to silence anyone. It is true that their boss is Donald Trump, so they did their job. I was presented with a tricky conundrum,” she said.

“The joke was already leaked by someone that was in the audience, a journalist or something. It was already in People magazine … But then they said, ‘We need to cut it from the broadcast.’ I’m like, ‘Well, it’s already out there.’ Who cares?”

Netflix later clarified that it was not behind the joke being cut, with a spokesperson telling The Hollywood Reporter: “While it’s our preference not to cut jokes from anyone’s set, The Kennedy Center has the contractual right to do so.”

Meanwhile, a spokesperson from the Kennedy Center told the publication that “edits to a show are always made in a collaborative way to produce the best product for broadcast”.

Cummings waded into the discourse again on Tuesday, writing on X: “I was super clear that Netflix did not cut anything from my Mark Twain prize set. Netflix always supports comedy and comics. Quit spreading rumors ya weirdos.”

Davis Ingle, a White House spokesman, told The Independent: “Nobody in their right mind cares what out-of-touch, woke Hollywood celebrities have to say.”

The Independent has contacted the Kennedy Center and Netflix for comment.

Cummings hosted this year’s ceremony, which honoured Maher with the help of Woody Harrelson, Arianna Huffington, Jay Leno, John Mellencamp, Louis CK and others. Previous recipients of the award have included Conan O’Brien, Kevin Hart, Adam Sandler, Jon Stewart, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Whoopi Goldberg and Richard Pryor.

open image in gallery Bill Maher receives the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor ( Reuters )

While one of Cummings’ jokes was cut, she was able to take a pop at Trump a few times during the streamed special. “I’m just glad that we could all celebrate Bill even though Trump is now the board chair of this venue,” she said at one point. “He actually does have a lot of power here and he has a say in what productions go on here, so enjoy this fall’s three-month run of white Hamilton.”

In March, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt reportedly told The Atlantic that rumours of Maher receiving the Mark Twain Prize were “fake news”, adding: “Bill Maher will NOT be getting this award.”

While the rumours ultimately proved to be true, the White House’s response may have had something to do with Maher consistently mocking Trump on his late-night show for over a decade. He previously joked that Trump was the “love child” of an orangutan and a human woman, resulting in Trump suing him for $5m in 2013 before withdrawing the lawsuit.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Chelsea bid rejected, Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal and Man Utd blow
Sports.content:
Manchester United, Arsenal and Liverpool are looking to get busy in the transfer market, while Chelsea completed the biggest deal of the summer in landing Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa

Welcome to Mirror Football 's live transfer blog for Wednesday, July 22.

There's a month to go until the Premier League returns, and with pre-season getting underway across the division, the transfer action is picking up. Chelsea completed a deal to sign England star Morgan Rogers after footing up a £117million fee to set the pace for the summer.

Manchester United have already been busy reinforcing their midfield with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, both arriving at Old Trafford. The Red Devils' business doesn't seem likely to end there as they remain linked to signing a new full-back such as Lewis Hall or Neco Williams.

Arsenal are set to welcome Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, but their bid to sign Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes is stealing the headlines. The Magpies remain adamant that their captain is not for sale but could they see an Alexander Isak repeat?

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, meanwhile, has said that Alexis Mac Allister and Alisson Becker will both remain at Anfield. The Reds prefer to add to their squad as they remain in the chase for Yan Diomande.

Sports.title: Anthony Taylor's biggest controversies, huge career earnings and real reason for quitting
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor's biggest controversies, huge career earnings and real reason for quitting

Anthony Taylor has been involved in some controversy moments as well as refereeing on the biggest stage

View 4 Images Anthony Taylor went out on a high, taking charge of the World Cup clash between Portugal and Spain (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

One of English football's most respected referees, Anthony Taylor, has announced his sudden retirement following a career spanning 20 years and more than 800 games. The Manchester official, 47, officiated 668 professional domestic games and oversaw every major English cup final.

‌



Taylor, who was promoted to the Premier League in 2010, refereed at four major tournaments, including the last two World Cups and at the 2020 and 2024 European Championships.

‌



In all, he took charge of 163 international matches and his final game was this month's World Cup last-16 tie between Portugal and Spain. Taylor said: "I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants Gary [Beswick] and Adam [Nunn], my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years.

‌



"Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Controversies

Like any top referee, Taylor has come under fire from managers, players and fans at times during his career. In 2023, he was confronted by Jose Mourinho in a car park following Roma's penalty shootout defeat to Sevilla in the Europa League final in Budapest.

‌



Taylor and his family were then harangued by Roma fans at Budapest Airport. He subsequently told his family to stop coming to his games, saying: "That's for sure the worst situation I've dealt with in terms of abuse.

Premier League referee Anthony Taylor retires from football and teases what's next READ MORE :

Reason why two English referees have been banned from officiating the World Cup final READ MORE :

"Not only because I was travelling with family members at the time, but it also highlights the impact of people's behaviour on others. It makes you reflect back on whether you made a mistake travelling with your family in the first place."

Mourinho, Roma's manager at the time, was charged with using insulting or abusive language and banned for four matches by UEFA.

‌



Taylor was the man in the middle during the Euro 2020 match in which Christian Eriksen collapsed from cardiac arrest. Taylor was praised for his calmness and the speed at which he stopped the match and called for medical attention.

At the following Euros in Germany, Taylor was criticised for failing to award the host nation a penalty in their quarter-final against Spain. Taylor played on after Jamal Musiala's shot was blocked by the arm of Marc Cucarella, with his decision not to award a spot-kick backed by VAR . However, a subsequent UEFA report said Taylor had erred by not awarding the penalty.

View 4 Images Jose Mourinho fumed at Taylor during and after the 2023 Europa League final (Image: PA)

‌



Taylor has had his moments of controversy in the Premier League as well. In September 2024, he dished out a record 14 yellow cards during Chelsea's match against Bournemouth and was demoted to fourth official duty the following week.

Taylor suffered another demotion in 2023, this time to the Championship, after he was deemed to have got it wrong by awarding Newcastle a penalty in a 2-2 draw with Wolves. The following week, instead of a Premier League game, he took charge of Preston vs Coventry at Deepdale, before returning to Premier League action.

Given his longevity and the scrutiny on referees, avoiding controversy was impossible. Taylor was widely regarded as one of the best and vied with Michael Oliver to take charge of English football's biggest games.

‌



View 4 Images Germany players appeal to Taylor during the Euro 2024 quarter-final against Spain (Image: James Baylis - AMA/Getty Images)

Premier League pay

Having spent 16 years refereeing in the English top flight, Taylor will have benefited from the burgeoning pay for officials. While not in the same league as the players he was taking charge of, he will have been earning around £250,000 per year at the time of his retirement.

While the average wage of a Premier League referee is around the £180,000 mark, as one of the best and most experienced officials, he will have been one of the top earners. Those figures do not include match fees, which exceed £1,000 per game.

‌



Taylor will have worked his way up the pay scale during his time in the Premier League. A conservative estimate would put his top-flight earnings at over £2.5m. He will have received one final match refereeing payday at the World Cup, where officials can earn up to £75,000.

View 4 Images Taylor issues one of his 14 yellow cards during a match between Chelsea and Bournemouth (Image: Ryan Hiscott/Getty Images)

Retirement reason

While Taylor's sudden decision has surprised many within the game, his statement referenced the pressure and scrutiny that come with being a top-tier official.

‌



He said: "Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career."

The last part of that statement suggests he has already planned his next move. Various roles could open up to him if he follows in the footsteps of the likes of Webb and Mark Clattenburg, who have both held lucrative positions in Saudi Arabian football. Webb has also previously worked with the MLS in the US.

Sports.title: England star set for awkward reunion after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap controversy
Sports.content:
England star set for awkward reunion after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap controversy

Jude Bellingham's actions at the World Cup mean one of his England team-mates may be in store for a very awkward run-in when he returns to club duties

View 2 Images Valentin Barco of Argentina (Image: Jose Hernandez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

England star Reece James has a rocky reunion in store once he returns to Stamford Bridge thanks to Jude Bellingham. That looks certain to be the case unless new £34million Chelsea signing Valentin Barco has a sudden change of character.

‌



Bellingham, 23, found himself at the centre of Argentina's scorn after bowing out to Lionel Scaloni's squad in the World Cup semi-finals. The Real Madrid superstar reacted to a comment from Argentina substitute Barco during their celebrations and gave him a slap on the back of the head in retaliation.

‌



Those actions led to a short-lived scuffle between the two sets of players. However, it's no longer his problem as Barco prepares to complete a summer transfer to Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg.

‌



Instead, the role of peacemaker will fall to Blues captain James, whose job it will be to integrate Barco into the squad this summer. And new manager Xabi Alonso will also have a task on his hands ensuring all those at the club with English connections get along with their newest team-mate.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barco, 21, previously made himself a target for England after storming the pitch to celebrate one of Argentina's comeback goals in Atlanta. The left-sided star intentionally ran in the faces of England's players in a mocking fashion before the Three Lions conceded their second.

‌



Chelsea to announce £34m transfer after Jude Bellingham World Cup slap READ MORE :

Full list of Argentina's 11 biggest World Cup controversies as punishments emerge READ MORE :

This was followed by the unused substitute running to join the revelry with the rest of his squad at the full-time whistle. And it was here his comment in Bellingham's vicinity drew a physical reaction from Thomas Tuchel's No. 10.

Barco's wife, Yaz Juareguy, slated Bellingham for his outburst and called him "useless" in a social media post after the game. She went on to suggest: "It's better to do the talking on the field."

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham was involved in an altercation with Argentina defender Valentin Barco after the World Cup semi-final. (Image: BBC iPlayer)

‌



Morgan Rogers, Chelsea's new record signing, may also feel a certain way about Barco's actions as they both join Alonso's side this summer. The former Aston Villa man is good friends with Bellingham and may not warm quickly to his new team-mate following his actions.

Trevoh Chalobah is the third and final member of the Chelsea squad who was on England duty this summer. However, the centre-back has been linked with a potential return to Crystal Palace, where he was previously on loan.

Sports.title: Liverpool facing more Real Madrid transfer frustration as Jose Mourinho eyes Reds target
Sports.content:
Liverpool facing more Real Madrid transfer frustration as Jose Mourinho eyes Reds target

Liverpool want to sign another centre-back before the summer transfer window closes, but Andoni Iraola's plans could be scuppered by Real Madrid and Jose Mourinho

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho wants more signings (Image: Antonio Villalba/Real Madrid via Getty Images)

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho is eyeing a move for Liverpool target Nico Schlotterbeck. The Borussia Dortmund star is high on Real's shortlist as Mourinho urges them to sign a left-footed centre-back.

‌



Schlotterbeck, 26, was heavily linked with Liverpool last season, only to sign a new contract with Dortmund in April. The deal, which runs until 2031, seemed to put to bed any speculation over his future before he jetted off to the World Cup.

‌



But Sky Germany now report that the contract includes a release clause worth between £42million and £51m. It's added that Real are have shortlisted Schlotterbeck, who Mourinho is a big fan of, alongside Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori, who can also play as a left-back.

‌



It wouldn't be the first time that Real have scuppered Liverpool's plans. In each of the past two summers, a player has rejected the offer of a new contract at Anfield in favour of moving to Madrid on a free transfers; firstly Trent Alexander-Arnold and then Ibrahima Konate.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Liverpool supporters will also recall Real beating them to the signing of Aurelien Tchouameni in 2022. And now Mourinho's plans could force the Reds to look for alternatives at centre-back.

‌



Andoni Iraola has already welcomed £60million signing Jeremy Jacquet to his defence and will get to work with the highly rated Giovanni Leoni, who arrived last summer only to suffer an ACL injury. But the new Liverpool manager admitted on Tuesday that they're 'very thin' when it comes to defensive options.

"With the centre-back, with the right-back situation, in terms of defensive depth, we are, I think, very thin right now, so I think it's a solution that we are trying to find, yes," Iraola told a press conference.

Should Liverpool bid for Nico Schlotterbeck? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Nico Schlotterbeck is on Real Madrid's shortlist (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto/Getty Images)

Liverpool could also sign a right-back depending on how Conor Bradley recovers from the knee injury which has kept him out since January. "I think it depends on Conor's situation," Iraola added.

"At the end if you have a fully fit, healthy Conor Bradley, we are very happy, ready to go and we would not be asking ourselves these questions. I think it's a situation that is tricky, because we trust Conor in the long term, we know we want him to be our right-back but right now he is still, I would say, a little bit far from returning."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's World Cup 'guarantee' to Donald Trump as he's told to resign
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's World Cup 'guarantee' to Donald Trump as he's told to resign

FIFA President Gianni Infantino enjoys a close relationship with United States President Donald Trump and they stayed in close contact during a controversial World Cup

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino offered Donald Trump a guarantee (Image: Eduardo Carmim/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino guaranteed Donald Trump that he would look into United States star Folarin Balogun's expected ban during the World Cup. The US President revealed that he contacted the FIFA president in a bid to resolve the situation.

‌



Balogun was sent off in the United States clash against Bosnia and Herzegovina, but was allowed to feature in the nation's next match against Belgium when the authorities chose not to ban him and instead offered him a suspended punishment and a fine.

‌



Infantino had already contacted FIFA’s chief legal and compliance officer, Emilio García Silvero, when he offered his guarantee to Trump, per talkSPORT. It is said to have been made clear to Silvero that reviewing Balogun's red should be a high priority.

‌



Opening a disciplinary panel was soon permitted, and from there Infantino stepped back to allow the process to run its course. However, it is has not been made clear that the review was deemed to be allowed.

For his part, Trump has bragged about his role, and enjoys a close relationship with Infatino which included frequent contact during the tournament. “I was forced to call Gianni and just make a recommendation,” said Trump at a fan event, with Infantino alongside him. “I said ‘Gianni, let the guy in the game!’

2034 World Cup could be delayed until following year as FIFA face Saudi Arabia dilemma READ MORE :

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

"No, I didn’t say that [laughter]. I said, ‘Gianni, I’d like to wage a complaint’. And I had no idea what was going to happen.

‌



"But it was so much better the way it worked out because there’s no controversy. They [Belgium] won the game, and our team had all its players… Gianni made yet another of his many good decisions."

View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino presented the World Cup trophy to Spain captain Rodri. (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The United States were ultimately knocked out by Belgium anyway, and the result escaped the Pandora's box that would have been opened had the Red Devils been knocked out.

Despite such controversy, Infantino was full of praise for the World Cup in the final days of the tournament. “This is the greatest human, social and cultural event mankind has ever witnessed,” Infantino said.

“For this, I thank you. One country will be world champion, but the world has already won, America has won, FIFA has won.”

Trump has reportedly given Infantino his backing to become the next United Nations Secretary-General. The Apprentice star is said to believe that the Italian would be perfectly suited to the role.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres 'not trusted' at Arsenal and Mikel Arteta's warning as transfer swap mooted
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres 'not trusted' at Arsenal and Mikel Arteta's warning as transfer swap mooted

Viktor Gyokeres' future has been questioned just a year after joining Arsenal

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres had an up and down first season at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Viktor Gyokeres has been suggested as a potential makeweight amid Arsenal's interest in Julian Alvarez. The Gunners are among the clubs interested in the Argentina striker, who has made it clear he wants to quit Atletico Madrid.

‌



Real Madrid and Barcelona are interested in the prolific frontman but Atleti are reluctant to do business with their La Liga rivals, meaning a move to the Premier League cannot be ruled out. English interest is led by Arsenal, just a year after they finally landed Gyokeres following a drawn-out transfer saga with Sporting CP.

‌



The Swede helped Arsenal to the title with 14 league goals, a respectable but not prolific return. Gyokeres had his detractors for his alleged lack of influence outside the penalty area, prompting some to wonder whether he should be the Gunners' first-choice number nine long term.

‌



According to talkSPORT, Arsenal have considered offering Gyokeres as part of a swap deal to land Alvarez. With that in mind, here's a round-up of his mixed first season at the Emirates…

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arteta's blunt warning

Mikel Arteta made it clear to Gyokeres that he must be able to handle a goal drought if he is to be a hit at Arsenal. Following an underwhelming opening few months, the Spanish insisted he could accept lean spells in front of goal, provided it didn't undermine his wider contribution to the side.

‌



Mikel Arteta stands at Arsenal crossroads as he weighs up huge transfer dilemma READ MORE :

Arsenal strike £34million transfer agreement for Greek winger Christos Tzolis READ MORE :

He said: "I told him before the first meeting, I said, 'The nine that I want is a nine that when he doesn't score for six or eight games, he can handle that. If not, you have to go somewhere else because the expectation is going to be there.

"So, if you put on a nine shirt for Arsenal, you have to be able to say, 'OK, six games, if I don't score, I'm a different player? I start to act in a different way?' No, I want much more of the same of what he's doing.

"You see the history of the number nines. You're going to have moments like this. He brings so much to the team. He creates space and solutions to a lot of the players around him. And with the talent that we have in the team, I'm sure that everybody, him included, will benefit from that."

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta made it clear what he expects from Gyokeres (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

'Not trusted'

Gyokeres' cause wasn't helped by Paul Merson's mid-season claim that he wasn't "trusted" by his new team-mates. In February, during an appearance on Stick to Football, the Gunners legend suggested players were reluctant to give Gyokeres the ball.

He said: "I watch Gyokeres, Arsenal don't trust him, the players. They never pass to him, you watch him, next time he comes short they go 'no.'"

‌



Merson added: "If you watch it, you'd be surprised, then when [Gabriel] Jesus comes on, they keep on giving it him all the time. That's what I see when I watch the game.

"He [Gyokeres] comes short and they never give him it. He makes some good runs as well. He's low [on confidence] at the moment but I don't think they trust him at all."

View 3 Images Merson reckons Arsenal players were reluctant to pass to Gyokeres (Image: Getty)

‌



Training ground behaviour

However, comments from Gunners defender Cristhian Mosquera indicated that he is highly rated by his team-mates. Following his slow start to the season, Cristhian Mosquera jumped to his defence, calling him an "animal" in training.

The Spanish defender told AS : "Gyokeres is a beast, an animal. Training with him helps defenders improve. There were great players at [former club] Valencia, but training with such high-level players is a huge leap forward."

Sports.title: 2034 World Cup could be delayed until following year as FIFA face Saudi Arabia dilemma
Sports.content:
2034 World Cup could be delayed until following year as FIFA face Saudi Arabia dilemma

Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup and while the tournament had been widely expected to take place in winter months like for the Qatar edition, there could be an even bigger change

View 2 Images The 2026 World Cup is in the history books (Image: Evrim Aydin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The 2034 World Cup hosted by Saudi Arabia could end up taking place in 2035 after FIFA were left with a dilemma. FIFA confirmed 18 months ago that the Gulf nation would host World Cup in eight years' time, and it'd been widely expected that the tournament would take place in November and December - like when Qatar hosted in 2022 - due to extreme heat concerns.

‌



But in 2034, there's a catch. Ramadan is anticipated to take place between November 12 and December 12, putting it squarely in the window which Qatar used.

‌



In Muslim countries, Ramadan drastically changes the way of day-to-day life, with social, civic and work schedules altered as a result. The millions of people observing Ramadan - held in the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar - fast during daylight hours and it's customary to avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public during these hours.

‌



This would no-doubt make it difficult for a World Cup to be staged during Ramadan, as thousands of fans flock to the host nation to watch matches scheduled throughout the day, while players and staff observing Ramadan would also be fasting. In 2022, Ramadan took place much earlier in the year and there were no such obstacles.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Donald Trump backs Gianni Infantino for shocking new job after FIFA World Cup backlash READ MORE :

But ahead of Saudi Arabia hosting, FIFA face a headache. A move to January and February of 2034 would see the tournament clash with the Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City.

‌



In early March of 2034, millions are set to make the journey to Mecca in Saudi Arabia for Hajj. The summer months will likely be avoided due to extreme heat, with the average temperature for Saudi in July being between 40 and 45 degrees Celsius - a worthy case for hydration breaks.

Given that the World Cup needs at least a five-week stretch, especially if the tournament is expanded from 48 teams to a whopping 64, finding a suitable period isn't easy. But there's one window which might - albeit reluctantly - suit all parties: January and February 2035.

This would allow both the Christmas and New Year period to be observed and ensure that the football concludes before Hajj, which in 2035 is slated to take place in mid-February. A 2035 date would, of course, mean that the tournament wouldn't take place in its usual four-year cycle, albeit by only a month or so.

‌



Should the World Cup be played in winter? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is opened-minded about changing the World Cup schedule (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Fans will recall how Euro 2020 was pushed back to 2021 due to the global pandemic. Having the World Cup in winter caused plenty of outrage within the European football community back in 2022, as top divisions such as the Premier League were put on hold for a month.

‌



But FIFA President Gianni Infantino believes that his organisation need to 'keep an open mind' when it comes to scheduling. "We are already into the nitty-gritty, we are discussing all the time," Infantino explained.

"It's not just about one World Cup, it's a general reflection. The best month to play football, which is June, is not used very much in Europe.

"Maybe there are ways we can optimise the calendar, but we are discussing it and we will see when we come to some conclusions. We just have to keep an open mind."

Sports.title: 'Silly Mr Bodybuilder!' - Fury casts doubt over Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says he is prepared to "fight somebody else" at the end of 2026 if his long-awaited showdown with Anthony Joshua does not go ahead.

Fury is fighting this Friday in Thailand against Poland's Mariusz Wach, although the fight will not be broadcast, before Joshua fights on Saturday against Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia.

Should Fury and Joshua win their warm-up fights, they have agreed to finally meet each other in November or December later this year - although a date and venue is yet to be announced.

However, speaking to Dev Sahni on Sky Sports News, Fury cast doubt on the fight with Joshua in an expletive rant about his compatriot.

"Let's not make this about silly Mr Bodybuilder. I'm not interested in him or his mates or anybody else. I don't give a **** about him. I don't care if I ever see him again in my life. If I do, I do. If I don't, I don't," he said.

"I'm not interested in him, anybody should do for him - his manager, his wife, his sister, his cousin. No interest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Jones discusses the best iterations of former World champions Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua

"We have got five months left of the year, so I want to get this fella [Wach] boxed, do well, and do what I can.

"I know I can beat this fella. I beat this fella with one hand, and that's not to say anything bad about Mariusz, but I'm in good form. I could beat all of these heavyweights with one hand. But I'm in good shape. I'm in fine fettle, injury-free and I'm ready to rock and roll.

"There's five months to get another fight in before the end of year ends. And if it is your man Anthony Joshua, good. And if it's not, then I'll be fighting somebody else."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn backs Anthony Joshua to beat Tyson Fury when the British rivals finally meet later this year, insisting Wembley Stadium is the ideal venue for fans

Fury has no plans to watch Joshua's fight

Fury's fight with Wach on Friday will take place at around 4pm UK time in front of 1,500 spectators in Pattaya, with Joshua fighting on Saturday night in Jeddah.

Joshua attended Fury's victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov in April earlier this year in London but Fury will not travel to Saudi Arabia.

"I'm going home. I've got about as much interest in Anthony Joshua versus 'some Pringles' as I have of spewing that all over the floor. None. I'm going home. I'm not interested in AJ and his mate boxing," he said.

Asked if facing off against Joshua in Saudi Arabia on Saturday would send a signal to everyone that the fight is happening, Fury added: "You can send out as many signals as you want.

"You've been told for 10 years it's happening. It hasn't happened, has it? So don't hold your breath. I've always had my doubts. But if it happens, good. If it doesn't, also good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Turki Al-Sheikh provides an update on where Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua will take place. Credit: SELA.

Fury: Wach is a tough man

Wach was last a heavyweight world champion in 2012 but has continued to fight annually, although has lost eight of his last 12 fights.

The 46-year-old wants to "ruin" the plans of Fury fighting Joshua and Fury is not overlooking his opponent.

"It's going to be crazy but I'm looking forward to the challenge. It's going to be good," said 'The Gypsy King'.

"He's a tough man. He's a veteran, and he's been around the game 20 years plus. So he's a dangerous man, a big heavyweight and anything can happen. I've got to obviously be wary of him and be on my A-game and do what I do.

"I've been out here 10 weeks training, so I'm not left any stones unturned. I'm ready to go. I'm in great shape and I'm fit as a fiddle."

Sports.title: Why Hungary could ignite Hamilton's title fight against Antonelli
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari must "come and fight for the win" at this weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix while McLaren boss Andrea Stella expects the Scuderia to be "extremely competitive".

Ferrari and Mercedes have shared two wins each in the last four rounds although the Silver Arrows have had the upper hand on outright pace for most of the season.

Kimi Antonelli, who is now 45 points in front of Hamilton and 50 points ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship, was on flying form last weekend in Belgium, even overturning the misfortune of not being able to pit under a Virtual Safety Car to beat Charles Leclerc on Sunday.

However, Ferrari were closer than anticipated at Spa-Francorchamps which bodes well for the Hungaroring as the track features lots of corners and that should play into Ferrari's hands.

"I think in Hungary, the Netherlands we will see the Ferrari being back to probably being the fastest car we see in the corners there. Extremely competitive," Stella told Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium

Hamilton has a record eight wins at the Hungarian Grand Prix but five-second time penalties at the last two races mean he has not challenged for victory since his triumph at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix last month.

"I'm hoping we can be [competitive]. I need to come correct this week and make sure I deliver the way I know I can deliver in Budapest," he said.

"We have to come and fight for that win."

Why Ferrari might be the team to beat in Budapest

Ferrari have been the benchmark in the corners this year while their main weakness has been their power unit, although they have closed their deficit to Mercedes and Red Bull recently.

The last two tracks - Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps - relied on a strong power unit due to the long flat out zones but the Hungaroring is largely about the chassis.

Energy deployment, or a lack of, will not be an issue so the cars with the best chassis will be strong, so Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok thinks we could see a repeat of Barcelona - where Hamilton was victorious.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix

"Ferrari have been behind Mercedes if you look at the trend across the season, apart from Barcelona where I think Lewis Hamilton genuinely had the outright pace to beat Mercedes," said Chandhok.

"I think Ferrari will be very strong [in Budapest]. We saw in Barcelona the aerodynamic package and the cornering speeds of the Ferrari is very strong."

Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins added: "Hungary and Zandvoort (the first race after the summer break) are both tracks where the straight-line performance is not tested on these cars, or any car at all. Those are downforce circuits where you are trying to get the most out of the car through those corners and that will promote Ferrari."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton watches back his first Ferrari win at the Barcelona-Catalunya GP in the cool down room alongside George Russell and Lando Norris

Vasseur, Leclerc play down Ferrari chances

There were similar expectations about Ferrari heading into the Monaco Grand Prix in June, only for Antonelli to convert pole position into victory.

Leclerc said: "I think it's very difficult to predict the level of performance of every team. I recall very well what the overall feeling was before Monaco, and we arrived in Monaco and were underperforming compared to what everybody thought we would, so I think we need to be cautious.

"We just need to do our homework, just like we do at every different track. I think what we did particularly well over these last two weekends was to really make sure that we maximised our package, and that's the mentality we should keep for Budapest, without thinking about expectations."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc wins the British Grand Prix after the Safety Car was redeployed at the last moment for the final lap

But, Ferrari have brought upgrades to the car since Monaco which further improved their cornering performance. Nevertheless, Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur is also managing expectations.

"I think everybody will bring upgrades and we don't know the picture of the performance. Everybody is pushing," he said.

"You have a lot of performance in the execution on tyre management, tyre preparation, set-up, and the layout of the track. I think if we do the same qualify of job as this weekend, it will pay off, but it is not a given. It's not a given for us and not a given for the others. Each weekend we are starting from scratch.

"For sure on paper the layout like Silverstone and Spa are probably a bit more difficult than some others. But on the other hand, in Monaco, we are not shining. That means we have to continue to push, to keep the same approach and never think that it will be ease, because it is never easy."

Sports.title: Lingfield and Worcester host competitive Wednesday cards
Sports.content:
Worcester and Lingfield are the venues for today's racing, with National Hunt and Flat action on the agenda.

8.10 Lingfield - Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest trappy affair

Hilltop, Kaori and Mojito contest a trappy-looking Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap at Lingfield.

Top weight Hilltop is a consistent performer who ran another solid race when third over this course and distance in May and should give another bold bid off the same mark.

George Boughey's Kaori is a lightly raced type who is yet to win in five starts. She wasn't beaten far when third at Yarmouth and drops back to seven furlongs with the hope of more to offer under Billy Loughnane.

Mojito ran out an impressive winner on her penultimate run at Doncaster before disappointing when favourite at Salisbury and has a bit to prove here.

2.25 Worcester - Red-hot Regal Renaissance seeks a four-timer

Regal Renaissance seeks a fourth success on the bounce as she takes on eight rivals in this Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Chase at Worcester.

Jack Jones' in-form mare landed her final start for trainer Henry Daly in May and has two wins from two starts for her new connections. She stayed on strongly when outpointing Fringill Dike at Market Rasen and this looks a good opportunity to follow up despite a 2lb rise.

Harry Hope looks a danger for the Ben Pauling and Jones combination. He has an excellent strike-rate over fences and should strip fitter for his last outing at Stratford.

Axel Bleue scored over this track and trip 21 days ago and remains unexposed over fences.

4.00 Worcester - Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash

Last-time winners Media Mogul and Playful Fox clash in a competitive Dolphin Tec Handicap Hurdle at 4pm.

Media Mogul recorded a first hurdling success when challenging late over this course and distance last month and makes appeal as he heads into handicaps off a mark 105.

Playful Fox represents the powerful Skelton team and is another who arrives on the back of a victory at Stratford. That was his debut win over hurdles, and he looks well-suited to this two-mile distance.

Others to note include Jamie Snowden's Kernie d'Airy, who got off the mark at the third attempt over jumps here last month and is another who makes his handicap debut. Ez Tiger ran well in second over this course and distance last month and goes again today, with Bryan Carver retaining the ride.

Best of the rest

Back at Lingfield, Emma's Letter will be fancied to give Ed Dunlop and Billy Loughnane a positive start to proceedings in the attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (6.10pm). This three-year-old daughter of Saxon Warrior has only been nudged up 3lbs for success at Nottingham the last day and with only three rivals to beat, she could go in again.

An hour later, Dreamlover represents Richard Spencer and Phil Cunningham in the Follow @attheraces On X Nursery Handicap. Connections will be hoping a return to five furlongs will pay dividends for this gelding, who drops significantly down in class for this assignment. Romidijo found just one too good at Chepstow the last day and could also relish the drop in distance.

The 7.40pm Free Race Replays On attheraces.com Novice Stakes sees the 89-rated Asuka take on Coilltedudeisback and Yazoo. George Boughey's charge is likely to go off a very short price in the colours of the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid.

Watch every race from Worcester and Lingfield, live on Sky Sports Racing.

Sports.title: Southampton boss Eckert charged by FA over Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert has been charged by the FA with misconduct and potentially bringing the game into disrepute over the 'Spygate' scandal.

The EFL expelled Southampton from the Championship play-offs in May and handed the club a four-point deduction for the 2026/27 season after they admitted "multiple breaches" relating to the unauthorised filming of their opponents' training, including before their semi-final against Middlesbrough.

Southampton beat Middlesbrough and were due to play Hull City in the play-off final before Boro were reinstated. Southampton appealed the decision, but the punishments were upheld by a League Arbitration Panel.

During the Spygate hearing, the EFL only had the power to charge clubs, not individuals. The FA waited for the EFL process to run its course before launching its own investigation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Keith Downie explains how Spygate unfolded at Middlesbrough's training ground.

The FA has now charged Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1, during the period between December 2025 and May 2026, by "directing and/or observing" training sessions of Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough ahead of fixtures against those clubs.

Rule E3.1 states: "A participant shall at all times act in the best interests of the game and not act in any manner which is improper or brings the game into disrepute or use any one, or a combination of violent conduct, serious foul play, threatening, abusive, indecent or insulting words or behaviour".

In response, Southampton say they remain "fully supportive" of Eckert and will "continue to cooperate fully and openly with The FA".

Eckert has until Tuesday July 28 to provide his responses.

Eckert 'loved' spying information

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton boss Tonda Eckert 'loved' the information gathered by a junior analyst intern when spying on one of his team's opponents, according to newly released messages.

In June, Eckert said he took full responsibility "for everything that happened", apologising to players, staff and supporters.

At that time, Southampton chairman Dragan Solak admitted Eckert had made a "mistake" but said the club was "fully behind him", reaffirming their target of winning promotion to the Premier League.

In the written reasons released following the League Arbitration Panel's decision to dismiss Southampton's appeal against their punishment, Saints' conduct was described as a "contrived and determined plan from the top down".

Eckert "loved" the information a junior analyst intern gathered when spying on one of his team's opponents, according to messages used as evidence in the hearing.

The written reasons detail how analysts felt pressure to carry out jobs asked of them as a colleague had lost their job earlier in the season.

The panel added: "A reprimand is considered appropriate because of the way in which junior members of staff were put under pressure to carry out activities which they felt were, at the least, morally wrong."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports' Mark McAdam, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert reveals the challenges he has faced after the Spygate scandal that resulted in their expulsion from the Championship play-offs.

Eckert told Sky Sports News last week that he had received police protection amid threats during the Spygate scandal.

"It's been an emotional summer. I can't lie, obviously, when the news broke towards the back end of last season, it's tough. It's not easy in that very moment. It's not easy to look into the eyes of the players. They're just so disappointed, and so many emotions coming out.

"You get so many threats at one point. You have police protection at one point; you can't drive a car. It's tough to deal with that for the very moment.

"When things calmed down with time, and I went back home, different challenges at home, you have a moment to reflect. I think that over the months there's also been a lot of positives that we can take into next season.

"After a couple of weeks, that excitement comes back in to go again and show what we are about. That's been the feeling since coming back into the training ground. We are in the second week of pre-season now. Players have come back in very good shape, with a smile on their face and ready to go again."

Spygate timeline: How did we get here?

May 7: Middlesbrough make formal complaint to the EFL alleging a Southampton member of staff spied on their training session three days before their Championship play-off semi-final first leg.

May 9: Boro boss Kim Hellberg accuses Southampton of cheating after the first leg ends in a 0-0 draw at the Riverside Stadium.

May 12: Southampton charged with a breach of EFL regulations in relation to the spying accusations. Southampton request additional time to conduct an internal review.

The play-off semi-final second leg is played at St Mary's. Shea Charles' extra-time winner earns Southampton a 2-1 victory and a place in the Championship play-off final.

Emotional Hellberg hits out at "disgraceful spying", before Saints boss Tonda Eckert storms out of his press conference after being asked: "Are you a cheat?"

May 13: Photos allegedly showing the Southampton analyst near Middlesbrough's training ground released publicly.

May 14: It is announced the independent hearing to determine Southampton's fate will take place on or before Tuesday May 19. In a statement, the EFL say "the outcome of the disciplinary proceedings may yet result in changes to the fixture."

May 15: Middlesbrough publicly call for Southampton's expulsion from the play-offs. In a statement, they said: "In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final."

May 18: Middlesbrough players return to training as the outcome of the independent disciplinary hearing nears.

May 19: EFL announces Southampton expelled from play-off final after hearing.

May 20: Southampton appeal rejected.

May 21: FA confirm they will begin their own investigation into Spygate.

May 23: Middlesbrough lose 1-0 to Hull City in the Championship play-off final.

June 1: WhatsApp messages reveal Eckert "loved" spying information despite the concerns of junior members of Southampton staff.

June 2: Eckert takes full responsibility for Spygate as Southampton owner Dragan Solak backs head coach.

June 17: Eckert tells Sky Sports News he received police protection amid threats during Spygate.

July 22: FA charges Southampton head coach Eckert with three breaches of rule E3.1.

Speaking in an interview published on the club's official media channels, Foden said: "Committing my future to City means everything to me.

"Playing for this club is all I've ever wanted to do and it's always an honour to wear the shirt.

"It's not lost on me that I've been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won, but we're always looking to the future and trying to win more.

"I can only thank the club, staff, team-mates and fans who continue to put their faith in me and trust that I give everything I can for City and I hope I'll be able to repay you for years to come.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports football journalist Laura Hunter says Enzo Maresca won't be afforded time to excel as Manchester City boss.

"I can't wait to work with Enzo [Maresca] again. He was brilliant during the Treble season - someone all the players respected and loved working with. To have him back here is exciting.

"Personally, I know I've improved so much from working with our coaches and world-class squad and as many of the legends who were here when I first broke through move on, I am excited for the next phase of my career at this great club."

Foden has made 369 appearances and scored 110 goals for City's first team since making his debut in a Champions League game against Feyenoord on November 21 2017.

Image: The 26-year-old has won 20 trophies with City

In 2025/26, he played 50 times, scoring 10 goals and providing seven assists.

Alongside John Stones and Bernardo Silva - who both left the Etihad this summer - the academy graduate is the most decorated player in the club's history, having won 20 major trophies, including six Premier League titles, one UEFA Champions League, three FA Cups, five League Cups, one UEFA Super Cup, one FIFA Club World Cup and three Community Shields.

Foden needs to reinvent himself - now might be the perfect time

Analysis by Sky Sports' Laura Hunter:

The curious case of Phil Foden, once a boy wonder, now somewhat of an afterthought. His omission from this summer's England group was expected but will have been no less dispiriting.

This is a player that England built their Euro 2024 bid around.

Since then, the 26-year-old has only exhibited flashes of his immense talent. Consistency has failed him. Pep Guardiola was forced to come to his aid a few times last season, insisting he's still a "top, top player", but it was clear he was no longer trusted to turn up in the big games.

Against that backdrop, a new deal seems bizarrely timed.

And yet, there is some logic to it. City have waved goodbye to Bernardo Silva this summer, leaving a big void in midfield. Guardiola himself is also gone. Foden still holds cohesive power, a player adored by fans because of his Mancunian roots and maverick style.

Now it's up to Enzo Maresca, who knows Foden well, to unlock the quality that resides within. This deal reflects the fact this next period has the potential to be Foden's peak years. A calculated risk, but one worth taking.
