Back in 2019, the FA issued formal warnings to the then Leeds manager Marcelo Bielsa and a club analyst for spying on Derby, but English football’s regulations have since been altered and tightened.

Sports.title: Financial ‘exceptions’ made for Pep Guardiola to become next Italy head coach
Sports.content:
Financial “exceptions” are in place to allow Pep Guardiola to become Italy’s next head coach, the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malago, has said.

Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of last season after winning six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the Champions League during a hugely successful 10-year reign.

He is free to take up another job, having also coached Barcelona and Bayern Munich, and has been linked with the Italy vacancy for some time, with it reported earlier this week that he has held talks with the FIGC. Gennaro Gattuso resigned from the post in in April after the four-time World Cup champions failed to qualify for a third tournament in a row.

“[Financial] exceptions have been made, exceptions that for example may concern the name that is so overbearing in these hours: Pep Guardiola,” Malago is quoted as saying by Gazzetta dello Sport. “Exceptions for obvious reasons that I am not here to explain, but it is not certain that this thing will go through.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Roberto Mancini, who led Italy to Euro 2020 glory, and former Azzurri midfielder Andrea Pirlo are other reported candidates for the vacancy. Asked if Guardiola, Mancini and Pirlo were the only names on the shortlist, Malago added: “Absolutely not. We think about a certain profile and certainly these names fall into that category.”

Sports.title: New faces, gulfs in class and flawed drama: how 48 teams changed the World Cup
Sports.content:
It was less than 12 months after Gianni Infantino succeeded Sepp Blatter as president that Fifa announced the expansion of the men’s World Cup from 32 to 48 teams. The reaction was mixed. Diego Maradona said he was “delighted by Gianni’s initiative” because it allowed each country to dream of reaching the tournament, renewing their passion for football. Joachim Löw, then in charge of world champions Germany, said: “I don’t think it’s a good idea to dilute the sporting value … In the long term, the quality suffers.”

On the evidence of the first 48-team edition, won by Spain after 104 games across five-and-a-half weeks in North America, it’s fair to conclude Maradona and Löw both had a point.

Cape Verde lead new faces

“Football is more than Europe and South America; football is global,” said Infantino after the 48-team format was announced in 2017, and the 2026 World Cup was undeniably a celebration of the sport’s diversity. Africa and Asia benefited more than other confederations when it came to greater qualifying quotas and all four debutants had their moments. Livano Comenencia’s equaliser for Curaçao against Germany was a group-stage highlight and Cape Verde were the tournament’s biggest underdog story, even if they didn’t win a game.

Adding the last 32 also gave six nations the opportunity to play knockout football at a World Cup for the first time, with Egypt and Canada recording their first such wins. With Infantino likely to spread the tournament’s record revenues across Fifa’s member associations, you could argue that the smaller nations – especially those drawing on a previously untapped diaspora – will only get stronger in future tournaments.

View image in fullscreen Egypt won their first World Cup knockout game, beating Australia on penalties. Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP

Gulf in class

With a bigger tournament came a wider disparity between opponents in the group stage. At the last 32-team World Cup in Qatar, Brazil versus Haiti was the biggest group mismatch, with a difference of 77 in their world rankings. In this tournament there were five group games with gaps of more than 65 places. Some of these were competitive – England 0-0 Ghana, Spain 0-0 Cape Verde. But there was little chance of a shock defeat for the big guns, let alone a humiliating group exit like those suffered by holders Spain in 2014 or Germany in 2018. A poor Uruguay were the only major early casualty this time around.

Whereas Costa Rica had the worst goal difference in 2022 (-8), there were five nations who either matched that or did worse in 2026. Iraq (-11) were the whipping boys in Group I – the closest to a group of death as the 48-team format could muster with France, Norway and Senegal, who all progressed in predictable fashion. The more pedestrian group stage did at least offer star names such as Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi a chance to gain some real momentum in a memorable race for the Golden Boot.

Flawed third-place system

After the drama of the 2022 group stage, where only two teams (about 6%) were officially out before the final round of fixtures, Fifa changed their plans for three-team groups for the expanded 48-team format and stuck with four-team groups, with eight third-place teams heading through to the last 32. This did not entirely bury the question of collusion between teams nor the fact that those playing later had a competitive advantage in knowing what result they needed to progress.

Knockout opponents could also change in an instant. When Riyad Mahrez put Algeria 3-2 up against Austria in the 93rd minute of the final game in Group J, it meant Algeria would go through as runners-up to play Spain in the last 32. When they conceded an equaliser in the 96th minute, it meant they would face Switzerland on the other side of the draw. Players and fans of third-place finishers like Scotland were also forced to hang around for several days before finding out they were, in fact, going home.

View image in fullscreen When Austria and Algeria met in Group J, the outcome (and therefore the last-32 lineup) was in doubt until the final seconds Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

With the shift from goal difference to head-to-head as a tie-breaker, there were five teams (about 10%) already eliminated before their final group game, the third-place system giving an illusion that everything would still be to play for.

What about 64 teams?

Infantino again stressed the importance of organising the World Cup “not just for Europe and South America” when he dropped the hint of an expansion to 64 teams. Adding an extra 16 nations – but only 24 more games – seems like a logical next step for Fifa if they want to do away with the third-place system and return to the top-two-go-through group format. There would at least be some jeopardy, although the disparity within the groups would be even greater.

Nations such as New Caledonia (ranked 151) and Indonesia (118) were involved in late-stage qualifying for the 2026 edition and could make it in with higher quotas. How would they fare against Spain or Argentina? And with the world’s 16 best teams all in the same pot, glamour group ties – which were already in short supply this time – would probably be a thing of the past. England 4-2 Croatia would not have happened with 64 teams.

Then there is the logistical issue of playing four games a day for a three-week group stage – with many matches taking place during the summer daytime heat in Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Of the 23 proposed venues, only the revamped Bernabéu and Camp Nou would have roofs. Further expansion will be a hot topic in the months to come, for sure.

Sports.title: England cannot afford trip to amputee World Cup – and the FA will not help
Sports.content:
Every time Scott Rogers walks into St George’s Park there is a sign on the wall that catches his eye. It boasts that the 330-acre site is the proud home of all England’s football teams. “I look at it every time and go, ‘Well, not all of them’,” Rogers says.

As head coach, Rogers guided the England men’s amputee team to the Nations League trophy in 2023. But while the Football Association funds six para national teams, amputee football is not among them.

Now one of the world’s leading amputee nations is struggling to raise enough money to compete at the men’s World Cup in Mexico in November. England earned £21.5m in prize money for finishing third in the World Cup and got £1.1m in preparation funds. The amputee side are trying to scrape together £50,000 to cover their tournament costs.

“The FA say they’re funded for a certain amount of para teams and at the moment there isn’t the funding to bring amputee football into the fold,” Rogers says. “We’re Nations League champions, and there’s a chance we won’t go to this World Cup. For an England team at the top of the game to miss a World Cup due to funding, it doesn’t sit right.”

The amputee programme was under the FA umbrella until 2006, when the governing body cut funding. “That left a lot of bad feeling at the time,” Rogers says.

They set up as a charity and have built a thriving structure. The women’s team reached the quarter-finals of the inaugural World Cup in 2024. The junior system has more than 70 players aged four to 17. They have doctors, strength and conditioning coaches, analysts, technical coaches. It is run by volunteers and funded by donations.

Rogers, a former youth coach at Wigan and Blackburn, became involved in 2000. “Whatever I’d do with an under-18 elite able-bodied team, I’d do with these lads because they were incredible,” he says.

View image in fullscreen Scott Rogers (fourth from left) coached England’s men’s amputee team for a year and helped them win the Nations League. Photograph: LAJ Photography

“When people think about amputee football, they probably imagine it’s slow and laborious. It’s the opposite: fast-paced, brutal at times. They snap crutches almost every game. I fell in love with it.”

FA representatives shadowed the team at the 2022 World Cup and were impressed. But though they made a funding offer, it fell short of what was in place. “All the signs were good,” Rogers says. But the offer would have reduced training frequency and cut the number of coaches and specialists. It was declined. Coming back under the FA umbrella while continuing to take money from other sources was not an option, Rogers says.

When Owen Coyle Jr – son of the former Burnley manager – stepped down as head coach in 2023, Rogers took over. Previously, players each had to raise £1,500 to secure their place for tournaments, but Rogers scrapped the requirement.

An appearance on ITV’s Good Morning Britain provided the funding boost to play at Euro 2024, their pot rising from £4,000 of their £40,000 target to more than £50,000 within hours. For the World Cup this year, they are not even halfway to the £50,000 needed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“These people don’t get paid for playing, they have jobs,” Rogers says. “If the programme isn’t of a certain level, what’s the incentive to continue to play? They sacrifice holidays with their families.”

View image in fullscreen Rhyce Ramsden (right) flies into an attempted tackle on fellow England amputee player Nathan Fisher (left) during a training session. Photograph: LAJ Photography

Rogers, who stepped down as head coach in 2024 but remains heavily involved, says even £50,000 a year from the FA would go a long way. “When you look at the funding within the FA and the money involved in football, what we’re asking for to make an amazing programme is a drop in the ocean.”

The amputee players are paying for their own flights for a game in Ireland next month. “It’s there, it’s ready to go,” Rogers says. “But the danger is if we don’t secure long-term funding soon – because we can’t keep going on telly, it’s a model that won’t continue to work – I feel that we’re going to start to fall away.”

Rogers says there are “brilliant” people at the FA who run the para programme and want amputee football included, but cannot secure the funding from above. “There are always ongoing conversations with the FA and it’s not a bad relationship. But unless something changes and somebody stands up and goes: ‘Listen, this can’t happen any more,’ I think it’ll be ground into the into the ground when we’re on the verge of something incredibly special.”

An FA spokesperson said: “We continue to work closely with the England Amputee Football Association to support, identify and help deliver their key priorities over the coming season, and the continued development of amputee football in England.”

Sports.title: ‘A unique talent’: Phil Foden signs new four-year Manchester City contract
Sports.content:
Phil Foden has signed a new four-year contract with Manchester City, saying he is looking forward to “trying to win more” at his boyhood club.

The fresh deal, which has an additional 12-month option, ties the 26-year-old to the club until 2030. Foden is relishing working again with Enzo Maresca. The new City manager was Pep Guardiola’s assistant during the 2022-23 treble-winning season.

Foden said: “Committing my future to City means everything to me. Playing for this club is all I’ve ever wanted to do and it’s always an honour to wear the shirt. It’s not lost on me that I’ve been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won, but we’re always looking to the future and trying to win more.

“I can only thank the club, staff, teammates and fans who continue to put their faith in me. I hope I’ll be able to repay you for years to come. I can’t wait to work with Enzo again. He was brilliant during the treble season – someone all the players respected and loved working with. To have him back here is exciting. Personally, I know I’ve improved so much from working with our coaches and world-class squad. I am excited for the next phase of my career at this great club.”

With John Stones and Bernardo Silva having left the club, Foden is City’s most decorated player with 17 major honours. The forward has won six Premier Leagues, one Champions League, three FA Cups, five League Cups one Uefa Super Cup and one Club World Cup.

Foden expressed disbelief at how long he has been at City. “Not in a million years [would I think this],” he said. “I would say I had a dream to make it to the first team, but to stay this long, it’s a dream really. And like I said, I’m just enjoying it and trying to make the most of it.”

Foden is hopeful that Maresca’s mode of play will suit him. “You can tell by the first few sessions that I’ve done with him – the way he likes to play out from the back and play a lot of possession-based – it suits my game really well. I’m looking forward to that and hopefully it can help my game go to the next stage,” he said.

The new deal indicates the firm belief of Maresca and Hugo Viana, the director of football, that Foden can recapture his form. He lost his starting place under Guardiola and was left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England World Cup squad. Foden’s form has fallen away since he was a key part of City’s 2023-24 title success and winning the Football Writers’ Association and Professional Footballers’ Association player of the year awards.

View image in fullscreen Phil Foden says he is hoping his game can reach another level with Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Manchester City

Last season, after the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on 4 March, Foden started only two league games and was substituted after 58 minutes of the 2-1 FA Cup final victory over Southampton. Foden has spent his whole career with City, joining as an eight-year-old.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Viana said: “Everyone at Manchester City is incredibly proud of Phil. He represents everything good about our academy. He is a unique talent, and his creativity is a joy to watch. None of what he has achieved would be possible without the focus, dedication and humility to work hard in every moment and absorb all of the knowledge available to him through our coaches and players.

“At 26, his development is still ongoing, and we look forward to seeing the player Phil can become over the coming years.”

After the 2025 FA Cup 1-0 final defeat by Crystal Palace, Foden revealed he had been struggling with off-field issues. He had also played with pain after suffering an ankle problem sustained from a Casemiro tackle in a goalless draw at Manchester United in April.

Sports.title: A tournament that crossed borders: crunching the numbers on the diaspora World Cup
Sports.content:
“Nationality says where you come from. And I actually come from four countries: France, Algeria, Nigeria and Great Britain. I consider myself very lucky to possess these four parts, which all enrich me.” This view was given by Michael Olise. He set up seven goals at the World Cup, breaking Pelé’s record for the most assists at a single edition of the tournament. And he did so for France, one of four countries he was eligible to represent, but not the one in which he was born.

The influence of players from the diaspora has never been higher at the World Cup. Four years ago, 16.5% of the players at the tournament were born in different nations from those for whom they played. That represented a 5.1% increase on 2018 and was the previous high for the tournament. No longer. Almost a quarter (23.6%) of the 1,248 players named in squads this year were selected by countries other than their birthplace. This proportion remained broadly consistent for the contribution these players made towards the minutes played, assists provided and goals scored. In a 48-team, 104-match tournament, these are big numbers.

There were 70 goals either scored or assisted by footballers born in countries other than the one on their shirt, with a further 19 both set up and converted by such players. As much as the World Cup has never featured as many games, six of the first eight editions saw no more than 89 goals in total, regardless of whether players were born in the nation they represented or not.

Not all goals are equal, though, especially at this level. World Cup moments become embedded within the collective consciousness of nations unlike almost anything else from any walk of life. All three host countries saw players born outside their borders make significant contributions. Colombia-born Julián Quiñones delivered the opening goal of the tournament in Mexico’s 2-0 win against South Africa. He scored in a further three matches, including in both knockout phase games that his team played.

Malik Tillman was responsible for two goals and an assist for the USA. When he was replaced after setting up a goal against Paraguay by Gio Reyna (who went on to score), it meant a German-born player went off for one initially raised in England. Players born in the US in turn helped their neighbours. Jonathan David spent his early months in the country yet became a Canadian hero by scoring a hat-trick in their first ever World Cup win. A total of 12 players were born in one of the co-hosting nations but in the squad for another country.

North America had nothing on France, though. Seventy-four players at the World Cup were born there without being on Didier Deschamps’ roster. While no squad can touch Curaçao’s for single impact from a specific other nation – with 25 of their 26 men being born in the Netherlands – the next five largest examples of one country providing players for another saw French-born footballers representing other teams.

There were 140 combinations of birthplace and team where the two countries differed, helping to illustrate how national borders matter less than ever before in this competition. There were even siblings who proved this point, with some experiencing wildly different campaigns. Nico Williams assisted the winning goal in the final for his homeland Spain, enjoying a better tournament than brother Iñaki, who only reached the last 32. His Ghana side were helped by a goal from Derrick Luckassen, the Amsterdam-born defender whose half-brother Brian Brobbey was the Netherlands’ joint-leading scorer this summer.

The Doué brothers were born in Angers, France, though while Désiré plays for the country, Guela represents Côte d’Ivoire. It’s a similar story in the Souttar family, with Harry (Australia) and John (Scotland) choosing different paths despite both being born in Aberdeen.

If one player sums up how the 2026 World Cup crossed borders in multiple ways like never before, it might be Nestory Irankunda. Born in Tanzania, he plays for Watford. The 20-year-old represented Australia and scored the opening goal of a victory against Turkey in Canada before he headed to Seattle to face the USA. His performances this summer have reportedly drawn the interest of Sporting, so he could be off to Portugal next.

Nationality in football has never been so complex, nor more readily blurred in international competitions.

Sports.title: Ally McCoist asked if he would replace Steve Clarke as Scotland manager
Sports.content:
Ally McCoist asked if he would replace Steve Clarke as Scotland manager

Ally McCoist admitted he would never turn down the chance to manage Scotland, as the hunt for Steve Clarke's successor continues.

Clarke immediately stepped down as Tartan Army boss after the national team's disappointing World Cup group stage exit, with no replacement being announced as yet.

5 Steve Clarke called time on his seven-year stint as Scotland boss after their World Cup exit Credit: Getty

After guiding Scotland to their first World Cup appearance in 28 years, the 62-year-old endured a difficult summer in North America.

His side finished the group stage as the 11th best third-place team and missed out on a place in the last 32 on goal difference.

With Clarke stepping down just moments after the nation's tournament fate was sealed, a number of names have been floated as potential candidates for the role.

So far, ex-Celtic boss Ange Postecoglou has been tipped for the role, as well as Everton's David Moyes, and recently departed Portugal manager Roberto Martinez.

Meanwhile, Clarke's assistant at Scotland, Steven Naismith, has also been backed to be promoted to the manager's role.

Can't say no

As speculation continues over who will be next to lead Scotland, the question was put to talkSPORT's very own McCoist over whether he would fancy his chances of taking the team forward.

The Rangers icon is no stranger to the Tartan Army dugout, having previously been assistant to the late Walter Smith between 2004 and 2007.

On Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast, presenter Shebahn Aherne quizzed: "In all honesty, Ally do you think you could do it?"

To this, McCoist quipped: “I'd need to give up talkSPORT for at least a couple of days a week would I not?"

Work commitments aside, the much-loved Scot insisted he would jump at a return to the national team set-up, despite not having managed since his departure as Rangers boss in 2015.

5 Steven Naismith was named Steve Clarke's Scotland assistant in August 2025 Credit: getty

5 McCoist worked alongside Scottish footballing icons in Walter Smith and Tommy Burns during his last stint in the national team set-up Credit: Getty

Answering honestly, he said: "I mean, they've got a bit of time to pick and digest and get whoever they want, but I don't know whether that ship's sailed, Shebahn, to be honest with you.

“I don't know, but you never knock back your country, do you? That's for sure, no matter what it is.”

On his previous spell with Scotland, McCoist said: “I loved it when Walter was in and he took Tommy [Burns] and myself as his assistants in the national team, it was one of the best periods, selfishly in my own life. I loved it.

“And Tam was obviously an absolute diamond, brilliant to work with and Walter - you know what I think of Walter - we had a great wee period there and the team did really, really well."

McCoist: Future is bright

McCoist was also enthusiastic about the prospect of the potential for a home European Championship, with England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland hosting the 2028 edition.

Due to tournament regulations, only two host nations are able to receive automatic qualification.

5 McCoist's last managerial gig came at Rangers between 2011 and 2014 Credit: Getty

But after Scotland qualified for each of the last two European campaigns, McCoist had plenty of optimism for the national team.

He said: “The great thing that we've got now, that we didn't have maybe about 10, 15 years ago, I wouldn't say the entire nation wasn't in love with the football team, but it had lost a little bit of love.

"That's back, it's clearly back and it's back in abundance. So we'll want to carry on.

“The next Euros are obviously in the home nations, so you clearly want to be part of that.

"I think there's two that qualify out of four and all that, and then if there's any other qualifications, a bit complicated, but you'd like to think we can qualify."

Ally's Scotland boss tip

After insisting he would always be open to the Scotland job, McCoist then claimed Falkirk boss John McGlynn could be in line for the role.

5 John McGlynn has guided Falkirk from Scottish League One to the Premiership in the last two years Credit: Getty

Three-time PFA Scotland Manager of the Year has been heavily linked with the role after guiding Falkirk to an impressive sixth-place Scottish Premiership finish last season.

McCoist explained: “I'm hearing John McGlynn at Falkirk has got a chance. I for one wouldn't think that was a bad idea, they did a brilliant job.

"They were brilliant last year, Falkirk and Motherwell in particular, were two great success stories last year. I've known John for a long, long time, he's just a good, hard-working, honest footballing man.

“We could do a lot worse than John, but I don't think there's any outstanding candidates at the moment.

“I think Derek McInnes would have been the obvious one, obviously before he got the Rangers job.”

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp set to appoint his former player as Germany assistant coach
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp set to appoint his former player as Germany assistant coach

Sven Bender is reportedly set to become Jurgen Klopp's assistant manager with the Germany national team.

The former Liverpool boss will be unveiled as Julian Nagelsmann's successor this week.



4 Klopp's Germany backroom team is taking shape ahead of his appointment as manager Credit: Getty

Klopp is understood to have agreed terms on a four-year deal through to the end of the 2030 World Cup.

It comes after Nagelsmann left the role following Germany's penalty shootout defeat to Paraguay in the round of 32 this summer.

Ahead of Klopp's appointment becoming official, his backroom team is now starting to take shape.



According to Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg, Sven Bender is in talks to become his assistant.

Negotiations are said to be in the final stages but nothing has yet been signed.



The former Borussia Dortmund midfielder will be joined by two of Klopp's ex-Liverpool staff members on his coaching staff.

Both Peter Krawietz and Pep Lijnders are also expected to join the national team set-up.



Meanwhile, Per Mertesacker remains in talks to become the German FA's new managing director.

Familiar face

As a player, Bender made 181 appearances for Dortmund under Klopp during his fabled time as manager.

The pair won two Bundesliga titles and reached the 2013 Champions League final together.

4 Bender won two Bundesliga titles with Dortmund during Klopp's time as manager Credit: Shutterstock



Bender also lifted the DFB Pokal in 2012 as part of a league and cup double for Klopp's side.

Having won seven caps for Germany, the 37-year-old retired in the summer of 2024.

He has previously worked with the national team at youth level as well as a brief return to Dortmund as Edin Terzic's assistant.

Bender's most recent role saw him manage Unterhaching to a third place finish in the German fourth-tier last season.



Klopp's task

As for Klopp, he is set to take on his first coaching role since leaving Liverpool two years ago.

The 59-year-old has been Red Bull's head of global soccer since the start of last year, with his deal running until the end of 2029.

4 Bender won seven caps for Germany during his playing career Credit: News Group Newspapers Ltd

However, it is now understood he will be unveiled as Germany boss at a press conference in Frankfurt on Friday.



His first match in charge will come away to the Netherlands in September as the Nations League gets underway.

Germany will also face Greece and Serbia in the competition ahead of the start of Euro 2028 qualifying next year.

Klopp is set to be tasked with banishing the national team's recent major tournament woes.

Their early World Cup exit this summer extended a 12-year wait for a knockout victory at the finals.



Germany have not won a match during the knockout stage since beating Argentina in the 2014 final.

4 Germany have not won a World Cup knockout match since the 2014 final Credit: Getty

Although they did advance from the group stage for the first time in three World Cups, Nagelsmann's side once again failed to reach the last 16.

Their recent record at the Euros has not been much better, with a round of 16 defeat to England in 2021 before losing to Spain in the quarter-finals on home soil two years ago.

Sports.title: How Argentina could line up at next World Cup without Lionel Messi as ex-teammate admits he may be finished with football
Sports.content:
How Argentina could line up at next World Cup without Lionel Messi as ex-teammate admits he may be finished with football

Lionel Messi has shown he can still play on a big stage at the World Cup, but he looks like he could be finished with football.

That is the opinion of Matias Fondato, who was at Newell's Old Boys when Argentina's captain first joined his boyhood club in Rosario.



8 Messi has been in three World Cup finals but has only won once Credit: Getty

Messi's international future has been plunged into doubt after he was unable to lead his country to back-to-back World Cup titles.

The 2022 champions surrendered their title following a 1-0 loss to Spain on Sunday after extra-time in a one-sided final.

That may be the last World Cup game for 39-year-old Messi, who broke down in tears after the defeat in New York.



Argentina's captain would be 43 by the time the next tournament rolls around, and Fondato feels he now looks like he'll walk away.

Messi 'could be finished with football'

"I've heard that the Finalissima is maybe going to be played in November or December, something like that," Fondato told Jeff Stelling and Gabby Agbonlahor on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"My hope is that he's still there for that game. But yeah, it's going to be very personal.

"If you ask me, if I see him still playing, I would say he showed everyone that he can still be for the big stages.



"But I don't know, it's going to be a personal decision. And you can tell that also he looks like he's done with everything."

Messi may not be the only key Argentine star to call it quits, with Fondato believing the Argentina squad needs a refresh.

8 Gabriel Batistuta, Mauricio Pochettino, and Maxi Rodriguez are all Newell's alumni, but everyone was speaking about the 'little magician'

"There might be a special situation of any player making it, but in general, yeah, there's a new generation of young players coming.



"Even the manager said that we need like a kind of renewal in all senses...

"There are some players that probably are not going to make it. I would say half of the team will still be at a decent age.

"I mean, even if they get picked or not are still on a decent age to play the next World Cup."

Argentina's XI without Messi

La Albiceleste's goalkeeper, Emiliano Martinez, had claimed he would retire from international football if Argentina went back-to-back.



While that didn't happen, the Aston Villa shot-stopper will be 37 by the 2030 World Cup and may be better suited to a back-up role.

8 It wasn't to be for Emi Martinez and Argentina this time round Credit: Getty

'Dibu' Martinez would only be a few months shy of his 38th birthday if Argentina again make a deep run in Morocco, Portugal and Spain.

However, River Plate's No.1 Santiago Beltrán will be entering his prime at 25 and was in Lionel Scaloni's thinking ahead of the World Cup.



Ironically, the now-21-year-old keeper has even been linked with a move to Villa Park to replace Martinez at both club and country.

Beltrán only made his senior debut in January but has already kept 13 clean sheets in 26 matches, and was handed his first Argentina cap during the pre-tournament 2–0 victory against Honduras last month.

Full-back was arguably La Albiceleste's weakest point at the World Cup just gone, but the country have several gems waiting in the wings.

Nicolás Tagliafico is already 33 - the same age Gonzalo Montiel will be in 2030, with Nahuel Molina and Facundo Medina both set to be in their early thirties for the next tournament as well.



8 Soler [right] played with current Argentina stars Almada and Alvarez at the Paris Olympics Credit: Getty

Palmeiras right-back Agustin Giay has been on the fringes of Scaloni's pre-World Cup squads, in a similar fashion to River Plate's Beltrán.

On the opposite flank, Julio Soler could make the left-back role his own if he continues to kick on at Bournemouth.

The 21-year-old made just five appearances for the Cherries last season, three in the Premier League, having arrived in January 2025.



The Paraguayan-born Argentine youth international, who starred at the Paris Olympics, was previously on the radar of Liverpool.

In central defence, Argentina may want to hold onto their tried and trusted partnership of Lisandro Martinez and Cristian Romero.

Yet both suffered injuries in the World Cup final, and may prove too big a combined risk when they come into 2030 at 32-years-old.

Instead, Chelsea's Aaron Anselmino will hope to have developed into a defensive leader after a promising loan at Borussia Dortmund.



8 Despite their flaws, Romero and Martinez have proved a great centre-back partnership Credit: AFP

Two of his Blues teammates could be a midfield option ahead of him, with Valentin Barco looking to make an impact on the pitch this time.

Alongside him will likely be Enzo Fernandez, who, at age 29 in 2030, will be desperate to atone for his red card in the World Cup final.

In Messi's absence, Como superstar Nico Paz could be trusted with the keys to Argentina's attack in his favoured No.10 position.



The 21-year-old Spanish-born attacker played just twice at the World Cup after a season in which he scored 21 Serie A goal contributions.

8 Paz has massive creative boots to fill if Messi decides to leave international football behind Credit: AFP

On the right, his ex-Real Madrid teammate Franco Mastantuono is a leading option to take the shirt after a stop-start international career.

The 18-year-old four-cap international became the youngest player ever to appear in an official match for La Albiceleste last year.



But Mastantuono, once viewed as a potential heir to Messi, was left out of Scaloni's World Cup squad following his struggles at Madrid.

Unless Alejandro Garnacho can make the most of his imminent Aston Villa lifeline, he looks to be destined to be left out in the cold again.

8 Garnacho chipped in with one goal and four assists from 24 Premier League games in the 2025/26 season

Thiago Almada is a contender to play on the left wing, but Argentine fans have a close eye on the emergence of Tomas Aranda.



The 19-year-old only made his professional debut with Boca Juniors in January, but immediately caught the eye of Argentina boss Scaloni.

So much so that Aranda was handed his maiden senior international cap in June and will be a key component for years to come.

Meanwhile, it looks to be a straight shootout between Inter Milan striker Lautaro Martinez and Julian Alvarez to see who leads the line.

The latter has the advantage of being two years younger, while a potential move to Arsenal would take his game to another level.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal reveals what Lionel Messi said to him immediately after World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal reveals what Lionel Messi said to him immediately after World Cup final

Lionel Messi had a heartfelt message for Lamine Yamal moments after the World Cup final.

The pair embraced on the pitch at the MetLife Stadium following Spain's win over Argentina on Sunday.



3 Yamal has revealed what Messi told him following Spain's World Cup final victory Credit: Getty

Ferran Torres' extra-time winner proved the difference as his side won the World Cup for the second time.

In doing so, Yamal added the title to his European Championship triumph from two years ago despite still being aged just 19.

The teenager ended the tournament with one goal and one assist in eight matches.



Although he missed out on the Young Player of the Tournament award to team-mate Pau Cubarsi, Yamal did receive a message from Messi.

The Barcelona winger has revealed what the Argentina captain told him on the pitch at full-time.



Messi had been slumped on the turf before standing up to hug Yamal as he approached him.

Messi's message

Speaking to Marca, Yamal explained: "He's the greatest player in history and someone I've always looked up to. After the match, I wanted to show him my respect.



"He told me to keep following my path and that the future belongs to our generation.

"Those words are worth as much as the gold medal hanging around my neck."

Comparisons have constantly been drawn between the pair through their Barcelona connections.

3 Yamal is a World Cup and European champion at just 19-years-old Credit: Getty



Both players have worn the No.19 and No.10 jerseys for the Spanish giants.

Yamal, who followed Messi in graduating from Barca's La Masia academy, finished second in the 2025 Ballon d'Or.

Meanwhile, a viral image from a 2007 UNICEF photoshoot showed Messi bathing an infant Yamal.

As a result, the 39-year-old became one of Yamal's footballing idols during his youth.



However, it was the youngster who came out on top in their first-ever competitive meeting in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Messi also missed out on the Golden Boot as well as failing to win a second successive World Cup.

3 Messi suffered final heartbreak as he missed out on winning a second World Cup Credit: Getty

He was beaten to the award by Kylian Mbappe, as he previously was in 2022, despite scoring eight goals and adding four assists in eight matches.



Mbappe ended the tournament with 10 goals for France following a brace in their bronze final defeat to England on Saturday.

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes could make immediate return to football action days after World Cup final controversy
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes could make immediate return to football action days after World Cup final controversy

Leandro Paredes could make his return to the pitch just days after his involvement in the World Cup final's mass brawl.

The Argentina midfielder was at the centre of controversy when Spain's World Cup triumph descended into chaos at full-time, as he launched into a violent rampage and threw punches in a wild scuffle.

5 Paredes threw punches and grappled with Spain's players in a violent rampage at full-time Credit: Getty

Ferran Torres' 106th-minute winner sealed victory for La Roja, and the 2022 champions lost all composure in the immediate aftermath.

Paredes was at the heart of this, who was seen attacking Spain's players as they celebrated as a series of bust-ups broke out.

Footage showed him grabbing Barcelona's Eric Garcia by the throat, before grappling with Gavi and throwing him to the ground.

This came after his Argentina teammate Nahuel Molina appeared to start the mass brawl by throwing a punch at Spain captain Rodri.

A series of altercations followed, with Paredes' actions the most violent, and it was reported at the time that he had been shown a red card for his actions, although the BBC later confirmed this had been removed.

But the Boca Juniors midfielder could still face punishment for this, with FIFA set to launch an investigation into the ugly full-time scenes.

Business as usual?

While Paredes awaits his fate amid huge criticism of his behaviour, he has already returned to his club side ahead of a quick turnaround.

Boca face O'Higgins on Friday in the Copa Sudamericana - South America's second-largest continental club competition.

And despite playing almost 700 minutes at the World Cup, Paredes could play in the game, just five days after Argentina's final defeat.

However, there are some concerns about the 32-year-old's availability, none of which relate to his post-match actions on Sunday.

5 Paredes is desperate to make a swift return for Boca Juniors, where he is captain Credit: Getty

5 The Argentina midfielder was in the thick of things as tempers boiled over at full-time in the World Cup final Credit: Getty

Paredes played the tournament whilst carrying a rib injury, which has left Boca weighing up whether or not to play him.

Reports in Argentina say the ex-Paris Saint-Germain star is desperate to feature, as he looks to put his World Cup heartache behind him.

As a result, Boca's medical team will monitor his situation throughout the week, before deciding if he is fit enough for the cup clash at La Bombonera.

Paredes speaks out

Despite being widely condemned for his antics after the World Cup final, Paredes is yet to address his involvement in the ugly brawl.

The 84-cap Argentina international spoke out for the first time since the ill-tempered New York finale on Tuesday, but made no mention of his violent rampage.

He wrote on Instagram: "Today, I write with a heavy heart, having been unable to bring our country the joy it so richly deserves - but with a chest full of pride for having given everything we had and for flying our flag at the very top once again!

5 Paredes addressed Argentina's World Cup final defeat - with the exception of the violent post-match brawl Credit: Getty

"Thank you to everyone who was part of this national team—to this group of players who gave their all to represent this jersey, fighting for it until the very last second of every match!

"It was an honour to be part of the best Argentine national team in history."

'Disgraceful'

While Paredes kept quiet on his role in the violent post-match scuffle, the rest of the footballing world has weighed in.

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor is among his critics, who insisted Paredes should be banned from the whole of the next World Cup.

The Aston Villa icon said on the talkSPORT Breakfast show: "You want to feel safe on the pitch, the punishment has to be that big that no-one ever does that again.

"No matter what happens in football, you can be angry you lost, but be classy in defeat, if you want to fight Paredes, there are places to fight - not on the pitch against Garcia.

5 Paredes turned on Spain's Gavi after he tried to intervene in his scuffle with Eric Garcia Credit: Getty

"And the way he was manhandling Gavi, a 21-year-old kid, and you were throwing him around on the pitch, that's someone's son, brother.

"Disgraceful. I would ban him from the whole next tournament if I had my way. Coward."

Sports.title: Wolves training ‘cancelled’ and ‘security increased’ as player refuses to leave
Sports.content:
Wolves training ‘cancelled’ and ‘security increased’ as player refuses to leave

Wolves have reportedly increased security to stop striker Tolu Arokodare from entering their training facilities.

It is claimed the Championship side were forced to cancel their training session on Monday after the Nigerian refused to leave the pitch.



3 Wolves had to cancel the entire of Monday's first team training session Credit: Getty

The club's new manager, Cesar Peixoto, has laid down the law and taken extra measures to ensure the 25-year-old does not return.

Wolves journalist Nathan Judah first reported the news and added that Arokodare will not be involved in the travelling squad for the pre-season friendly against Maidenhead United.

Why is Arokodare banned from training?

The 25-year-old moved to Molineux from Genk in 2025 for a fee of £26million.



However, Arokodare has been unable to replicate his Belgian goalscoring form in the Premier League, netting just three goals in 33 appearances.

This is not his first problem Wolves have encountered with the player. After the team were thrashed 4-0 by West Ham in April, the striker and Matheus Mane had a physical altercation in the dressing room.



Following that incident, the midlands-based club sanctioned the frontman and issued a fine.

The Nigerian has already informed Wolves of his desire to leave this summer; however, the Molineux hierarchy want more than €20million (£15million) for his sale.



Arokodare has made it clear he wants to continue playing in one of Europe's top five leagues after Wolves accepted a bid from Turkish giants Trabzonspor

Serie A side Fiorentina remain interested and have reportedly submitted an improved proposal of €22million (£16.5million) option to buy.

FIFA Repercussions

However, the entire incident could cause a headache for Wolves following FIFA introduction of new player protection rules last month.

3 Tolu Arokodare is under contract at Wolves until 2029 Credit: Getty



The updated regulations were designed to stop clubs from isolating players simply to force them out.

Clubs are no longer allowed to force contracted players to train separately from the main group to pressure them into accepting transfers.

Players must continue training with the first team unless there is a legitimate sporting reason or a documented medical issue preventing their participation.

If FIFA determines that a club has breached these regulations, the consequences can be severe. Players remain entitled to receive their full salaries and benefits.



They may also seek contract termination, allowing them to leave on a free transfer rather than generating a transfer fee for their club.

Laying down the law

Peixoto was brought in to replace Rob Edwards, who was sacked after the midlands-based outfit were relegated from the Premier League after finishing bottom of the table.

3 Peixoto is tasked with restoring Wolves back to the Premier League Credit: Getty

In the head coach's first interview, he said: "Firstly, I'm a very demanding coach. But, I believe in giving others maximum freedom and maximum responsibility.



" I want us to work as a team and as a unit and build a good environment.

"This is important to me, but I know very well what I want from the team. I want my team to be organised with and without the ball.

"Secondly, I want a team with intensity and to be aggressive and win duels.

"The third one is I want to show the quality of the players. To play an offensive game and to try and press high. To try and be the main character of the games.



"I want to win games, but I want to win while playing good football. With passion and energy.

"[The supporters can expect] a team with ambition. A strong character and identity and a strong idea of the game.

"A team that never gives up to win three points and to try and make the fans proud."

Sports.title: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert hit with three FA charges after Spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton manager Tonda Eckert hit with three FA charges after Spygate scandal

Tonda Eckert has been charged with three breaches of the FA's rules relating to spying on opponents.

The Southampton manager's alleged breaches relate to matches against Oxford United, Ipswich Town and Middlesbrough last season.



3 Eckert has been charged with three breaches of spying rules by the FA Credit: Getty

Saints were disqualified from the Championship play-offs in May after their spying offences came to light.

An analyst intern was caught filming a Boro training session ahead of their first leg meeting at the Riverside Stadium.

The two further spying incidents later came to light, with the club also deducted four points for the coming season.



Eckert has been given seven days to respond to the FA charges.

However, talkSPORT understands he is unlikely to contest them.

Southampton statement

Responding to the charges in a statement, Southampton said: "Southampton Football Club and First Team Head Coach Tonda Eckert acknowledge today’s charges from The FA relating to a breach of Rule E3.1.

"Tonda and the club will continue to cooperate fully and openly with the FA.



"Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026/27 Championship season.

"The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.



"We are unable to comment further while the process remains ongoing, but we will provide an update to supporters as soon as we are in a position to do so."

3 Eckert has been given seven days to respond to the charges but is not expected to contest them Credit: Getty

Saints begin the new Championship season away to Watford on Sunday, August 16.

Eckert's future

Eckert's future had appeared to be in doubt following the Spygate scandal, with his side blocked from appearing in the play-off final.



Having beaten Boro 2-1 on aggregate, their opponents were reinstated before losing to Hull City at Wembley Stadium.

However, Southampton owner Dragan Solak later backed Eckert to continue in the role.

The 33-year-old has been in permanent charge since December following a five-match caretaker spell at St. Mary's.

His current deal is due to run until the end of the 2026/27 season.

3 Southampton were disqualified from the play-offs and handed a points deduction for spying on their opponents Credit: Getty



Since being named as permanent manager, Eckert has won 21 of 35 matches in all competitions and suffered just five defeats.

As well as finishing fourth in the Championship last season, Saints also reached the semi-finals of the FA Cup.

Sports.title: ‘Stop judging’ – Emma Hayes tipped to become England men’s manager one day
Sports.content:
‘Stop judging’ – Emma Hayes tipped to become England men’s manager one day

Emma Hayes has been tipped to one day manage the England men's national team.

The former Chelsea women's boss could be a potential candidate for the FA in the future, according to talkSPORT's Shebahn Aherne.

3 Hayes has been tipped to one day manage the England men's national team Credit: Getty

Although current manager Thomas Tuchel has two years remaining on his deal, the Three Lions' World Cup exit has caused mounting pressure for the German.

Tuchel signed an extension through to the end of Euro 2028 in February.

As for Hayes, the 49-year-old won 16 trophies during 12 years in charge of the Blues, including seven Women's Super League titles.

Her side also reached the final of the Women's Champions League for the first time in the club's history.

Having left Chelsea in 2024, Hayes has since served as head coach of the USA women's national team.

She has since continued her previous success, winning Olympic gold in Paris two years ago.

Hayes tipped for England

Aherne has now proposed a potential appointment as Three Lions manager for Hayes once she leaves her current role.

Discussing the England post with Gabby Agbonlahor on talkSPORT Breakfast, she said: "We were talking earlier on about Pep Guardiola, if he were to possibly get the England job.

"I was actually thinking, I think some time soon you could see somebody like Emma Hayes get appointed for the England job."

Pep Guardiola is currently without a job having left Manchester City after nine years in charge at the end of last season.

3 Hayes won seven WSL titles during 12 years in charge of Chelsea Credit: Getty

The Spaniard is keen to manage England in the future, talkSPORT understands, having been tipped as a possible successor to Tuchel.

However, the FA could face competition from the likes of Saudi Arabia and Qatar to appoint Guardiola.

Impressive analysis

Meanwhile, Hayes is fresh from appearing as a pundit for ITV during this summer's World Cup.

Her analysis throughout the tournament in particular caught the eye of supporters.

Aherne was equally impressed, adding: "I think she really captured the nation, this tournament. I think a lot of people enjoyed her analysis.

"People like John Terry, Simon Jordan, you’ve got to spend time with this woman and understand her brain and maybe stop judging people on having worked with women.

3 Hayes has continued her success with the USA, winning Olympic gold in 2024 Credit: Getty

"And just being a world class coach, which she is."

Hayes has been backed for roles in men's football already in her career.

Gary Lineker even once contacted his former club Leicester City to urge them to consider appointing her.

She was also reportedly considered for the first-team manager's job by AFC Wimbledon back in 2021.

Sports.title: Former England star's son, 18, joins Arsenal after being persuaded to snub bitter north London rivals Tottenham
Sports.content:
Elijah Upson, the son of former England international Matthew, has signed for Arsenal after leaving Tottenham.

The 18-year-old turned down a professional deal at Spurs earlier this year and had offers from Chelsea, Manchester City, Everton, Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Leverkusen and Monaco.

But, after visiting Arsenal's training ground earlier this month and holding talks with his family, he has decided to join the Premier League champions.

He follows a similar path to his father, Matthew, who had two of his formative years with Luton Town before joining Arsenal for £2m as an 18-year-old.

Upson Snr played 57 times for the Gunners and won the Premier League in 2001-02, before he later represented England at the 2010 World Cup and earned 21 caps.

Upson Jnr, also a centre back, will hope he can build a similar career. He is quick, perhaps thanks to the fact his mother is former runner Ellie Darby, but also strong on the ball.

Elijah Upson has signed for Arsenal after rejecting a new contract offer from Tottenham

Upson is the son of former Arsenal and England centre back Matthew (pictured, right)

Speaking after his move was confirmed, the 18-year-old revealed he was attracted by the quality of defenders at Arsenal and the potential path into the first team.

He said: 'That was one of the big reasons for my decision - obviously it's great exposure to some of these great players that have had a great season here and some real top quality.

'I'm excited to hopefully be around and work with these people. I think definitely the centre-back partnership in the first team that there is between (William) Saliba and Gabriel, they're a good inspiration and really experienced, high-quality players.

'They've had a great season, definitely two players that I'm really keen to learn from and expose myself to hopefully.'

Upson Jnr later added: 'It's a great feeling, I'm really proud to be here. When I met the guys here recently and met all the team and staff, it just seemed like a really nice environment.

'That was probably the biggest factor, an environment where you feel you can hopefully learn and get better as a person.'

The defender had captained Tottenham at Under 18 level and also represented England at that age group.

In his welcome interview at Arsenal, he similarly outlined a desire for 'some exposure to the first team' this season and he is set to wear the No 57 shirt at the club.

Given Upson is under the age of 24, the Gunners will now look to agree compensation with Tottenham.

Sports.content:
Roma attempt to hijack Al-Hilal's £60m move for West Ham star Crysencio Summerville with last-ditch swoop - as Issa Diop makes £8.5m Premier League switch: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Morgan Rogers completing his £117m move from Aston Villa to Chelsea - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Roma's last-gasp Summerville swoop

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to choose them over Al-Hilal.

Coach Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Summerville last night to try and convince him Roma's project was more suitable for the Netherlands international.

Al Hilal have agreed a £60m fee with West Ham with £55m up front.

Roma had offered £39m plus add ons.

The Italians are also keen on Chelsea defender Axel Disasi who was a teammate of Summerville's at West Ham last season.

They also made an offer for Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho but Aston Villa's proposal for the winger offers more guarantees.

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to sign for them

Wober departs Elland Road

Leeds United defender Maximilian Wober is joining Schalke on a free transfer.

The 28-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen, has been having a medical with Schalke.

Van Hecke completes Spurs move

Fellow Netherlands international Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton.

The Dutch centre-half, who chalked up three goals and three assists from 36 Premier League match for the Seagulls last term, had one year left on his contract at the Amex before Spurs swooped in to sign him.

It marks the latest signing in what has been a busy transfer window for Spurs, with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Andrew Robertson, Martin Dubravka and Marcos Senesi all joining Roberto De Zerbi's ranks ahead of the new season.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough have confirmed the signing of striker Will Lankshear from Tottenham in a deal worth £20million including add-ons.

He has signed a five year contract and said: 'Middlesbrough is such a massive club over the years; I deem it to be a Premier League club.

'The project here really excites me. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the journey, and get this club back where it belongs.'

Lankshear scored 11 goals in 43 appearances for Oxford United last season and also had interest from Wolves.

Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton

Tigers see £13.6m Danois bid rejected

Hull City have had a £13.6million bid rejected for Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old, who is also on Newcastle United’s watchlist, has emerged as a top target for Hull but Auxerre value him closer to £25million.

That would require Hull to smash their club transfer record and they want at least two new midfielders.

Danois is a France U21 international and made 33 appearances in Ligue 1 last term, scoring three times and registering one assist.

Liverpool's swoop for Monaco star comes up short

Liverpool made an approach for Monaco attacking midfielder Maghnes Akliouche early in the window.

The club checked on the potential availability of the 24-year-old but it was evident he was a prime target for Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG have made offers to Monaco for the France international but have still to agree on the fee.

Liverpool did not progress with talks after their initial check and are exploring other options including PSG's Bradley Barcola.

Wolves outcast Arokodare poised for swift exit

Ajax have joined the clubs showing interest in Wolves' wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare.

Arokodare will not be part of Wolves' squad to face Maidenhead tonight after his actions prompted coach Cesar Peixoto to cancel training on Monday.

The Nigerian refused to exit the training pitch when asked prompting the session to be cancelled. Extra security was then called in to the training ground on Tuesday to ensure the 25-year-old striker did not disrupt the session again.

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry.

Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

In April, he faced disciplinary action after a dressing room bust-up with team-mate Mateus Mane during a 4-0 defeat at West Ham.

Wolves cancelled training after wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch

Diop makes Premier League switch

Ipswich Town have confirmed the signing of Issa Diop from Fulham in a deal worth around £8.5m.

The centre-back has signed a four-year deal.
