Although this is the highest figure on record, the Tourism Committee expects to break the record again by the end of the year. Officials expect the number of tourists to surpass last year’s total of 2.2 million visitors.

Main sources of tourist arrivals

According to the Tourism Committee, visitors from Russia, Georgia and Iran have made up the largest share of tourists travelling to Armenia for many years. As of June this year, that pattern had not changed. The figures are as follows:

Around 40% of all visitors came from Russia,

15% from Georgia,

8% from Iran.

Compared with the three leading source markets, visitor numbers from other countries remain relatively low. According to Sona Hovhannisyan, head of the International Cooperation Department, several factors explain why tourists from these countries account for the largest share of arrivals:

“Iran and Georgia are Armenia’s closest neighbours, while Armenia has historical ties with Russia. It is also important that people can travel to Armenia from these countries relatively quickly. The presence of Armenian diaspora communities in these countries also plays a role.”

Hovhannisyan said countries with direct flights to Armenia, as well as those whose citizens benefit from simplified visa rules, have seen growing numbers of visitors. She cited China as an example, saying the sharp increase in Chinese tourists followed the launch of direct flights between Urumqi and Yerevan, along with the introduction of a visa-free regime.

Hovhannisyan also explained what has driven growth from other countries:

“The significant increase in the number of tourists from Italy is due to the expansion of flights between our countries. The same factor has influenced arrivals from Germany, where visitor numbers had previously declined. The launch of a direct flight from Kazakhstan has also boosted tourist flows.”

Armenia has also recently become a more popular destination for tourists from Spain, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom.

Hovhannisyan said visitor numbers from those countries remain well below the figures for Russia. However, she added that the recent launch of direct flights between London and Yerevan gives reason for optimism.

“The peak tourism season is gradually getting longer”

Armenia usually sees the highest number of tourist arrivals during the summer and in September and October. Activity typically begins to slow towards the end of November. According to Hovhannisyan, however, the peak season is gradually becoming longer. She said more tourists are now choosing to visit the country during the winter months.

“It is encouraging to see growing activity during the winter as well. The government is taking steps to support this trend. If this January’s record figures are sustained and become the norm, we can expect strong tourism for almost the entire year.”

Trade fairs and other PR efforts to attract tourists

The Tourism Committee is running a number of programmes to make Armenia a more attractive destination on the international tourism market.

According to Diana Karapetyan, head of the Marketing Department, Armenia showcased national pavilions at major tourism fairs in Spain, Germany, Romania and Russia this year.

“By the end of the year, we plan to take part in several more international events. Armenian tourism companies attending these exhibitions present highly attractive offers. They promote our country’s cultural events, cuisine and tourist attractions. They also offer tastings, distribute brochures and show promotional videos.”

The committee also works with international media outlets, PR agencies, well-known bloggers and influencers. It organises familiarisation trips to Armenia and runs promotional campaigns. Karapetyan said these efforts have led to more frequent coverage of Armenia in the international media, with growing attention to its tourism appeal and potential.

“Armenia has established itself on the global tourism market as a safe and reliable destination,” she said.

Tourist arrivals in Armenia reach record high

World.title: 'Turning point' for housing market as property prices hit three-year low
World.content:
Australia's housing boom has officially entered a downturn for the first time in more than three years, with property prices falling from record highs in the June quarter.

The figures, released by online real estate company Domain, show that national capital city house prices fell by 1.4 per cent in the June quarter, while national unit prices dropped by 1.2 per cent.

While annual growth remains positive for both houses and units nationally, it has slowed to its lowest level in nine months.

The report noted that the change represented a "decisive shift in market conditions" due to higher interest rates, affordability constraints and waning confidence amongst buyers, while listings are increasing and homes are taking longer to sell.

Domain's chief of research and economics, Nicola Powell, said it marked a turning point for the nation's housing market.

"After three years of uninterrupted price growth we've got house and unit prices declining over the quarter, so that does indicate that we are now in a downturn," she told The Business.

But not every capital city saw a decline in house prices, with Adelaide the only city where prices accelerated in the June quarter.

Despite the downturn, house prices remained at record highs in the South Australian capital, as well as Brisbane, Perth and Hobart.

"It was a bit of a mixed outcome depending on the capital city; we're seeing declines in Sydney, Melbourne and Canberra, that's really leading the downturn," Dr Powell said.

" What we are starting to see is it is broadening out and actually, while other capital cities are recording growth, that growth is much slower compared to what we had previously seen. "

However, Dr Powell said the downturn trend was most evident in unit prices, where all capital cities except for Darwin recorded a fall.

"That was a surprise to us, and I think that really shows that investors have become nervous; they are shying away from the housing market, but it may be having a ripple effect on first home buyers as well," she said.

"I think there would absolutely be nervousness out there amongst first home buyers, that cautious approach, but I also think that behavioural response from first home buyers, thinking if they wait a little bit longer and prices pull back even further, they may get actually more for their money."

Before the publication of the Domain data, property economist Cameron Kusher said he expected national dwelling values to decline.

"I think this downturn is set to be one of the largest we've seen in many years … [and] will turn out to be larger than the 7.5 per cent downturn seen a few years back," he wrote on Wednesday.

"We have a somewhat perfect storm of low affordability, low sentiment toward housing, a weakening economy with productivity growth terrible, reduced incentives to invest in housing, relatively high interest rates and high inflation that looks set to continue for some time."

Unit prices declined in every capital city except Darwin in the three months to June. (ABC News: Declan Bowring)

A sustainable slowdown?

Mr Kusher, who stressed that his views were independent of his employer, said it was unlikely the falls would translate to housing affordability.

"With these declines in housing values, they won't improve affordability greatly because I expect that interest rates won't be reduced for some time and because dwelling values have increased by so much and so quickly over recent years," he said.

"Historically, downturns in the national housing market have been fairly short-lived, and the recovery has been driven by interest rate reductions and/or significant market stimulus, typically to first home buyers.

"The decline in values I am anticipating is likely to result in weaker household consumption, higher unemployment and eventually lower inflation, but that is all likely to take time.

"Whilst housing value declines are always framed as negative, they create opportunities too. Lower housing values afford new purchasers an opportunity to enter the market, they improve housing affordability, and they provide opportunities to transact.

" Just because your home may be worth less, so too is that property you are buying and right now the more expensive properties are seeing larger value falls so it may be an upgrading opportunity. "

Cameron Kusher says a "perfect storm" of conditions will see property prices continue to fall. (ABC News: Adam Griffiths)

On Monday, Barrenjoey banks analyst Jonathan Mott told a Senate Committee into productivity that a housing slowdown would have a positive impact on the sustainability of Australia's housing market.

"If we could have a situation where house prices were flat for 10 to 15 years in nominal terms and fell in real terms, improving affordability, that would be a great outcome for all Australians," he said.

Mr Mott noted that demand for mortgages had already been slowing for some months, referencing data that showed home loan applications had declined by around 23 per cent since the start of February.

"Within this, mortgage applications for first home buyers are down 19 per cent, owner-occupiers to upgraders are down 15 per cent, while investors are down 35 per cent, all seasonally adjusted," he said.

"It should be noticed that this is mainly as a result of a reduction in demand."

Now with a downturn in property prices, Dr Powell said it showed consumer confidence had been impacted, especially in the aftermath of the federal budget.

"Australians didn't really take the budget very well, and I think that's coming out," she said.

"Investors are pulling back, and I think people are just becoming much more nervous about the housing market.

" The housing market really is a confidence game, and people don't transact property if they're not feeling confident. "

Nicola Powell is the head of research and economics at Domain. (ABC News: Jack Ailwood)

Despite the decline, however, she said it would not be a catalyst for a correction or a crash in the property market.

"I think that's very unlikely because what you have is a pullback in new sellers coming to the market … people just wait, they pause their decisions until market conditions improve," she said.

World.title: Nina Kennedy arrives early to lead Australia into Glasgow opening ceremony
World.content:
Nina Kennedy will carry the Australian flag in the Glasgow 2026 opening ceremony before she tries to defend her Commonwealth Games pole vault title.

Kennedy is the first of the Australian athletics team to touch down in Glasgow, with the track and field program not starting until Monday.

"I am so proud to follow in the footsteps of so many great Australians who have carried the flag before me. The Commonwealth Games have always meant so much to me; it's where I won my first medal back in 2018," Kennedy said.

"This is my third Games, and I'm lucky enough to be defending my title. My final isn't until later in the week, so I'll get a bit of a sleep-in the morning after.

Do you know an athlete competing at the Commonwealth Games? Share with us Whether you are you a family member, a friend, a colleague or a coach, share your connection with us and how you will be supporting them.

"I've worked with our team to make sure I'm as prepared as I can be, and there's no version of the Games where I'd miss the chance to carry that flag."

Kennedy won gold in Birmingham after claiming silver four years earlier on the Gold Coast.

Since then she has broken the Australian record, become a world champion in 2023 and won Olympic gold in 2024.

A torn hamstring wiped out her 2025 season, including the chance to defend her world title last year, but she has returned to competition without missing a beat in 2026, breaking the national record for a 10th time just two weeks ago in Monaco.

"I've had a long road with injuries to get back to this point, so to be trusted with this now, on top of everything else so far this season, means more than I can really put into words," she said.

Kennedy will be joined by another reigning gold medallist, para swimmer Tim Hodge, who will carry the King's Baton at Friday morning's (AEST) ceremony at the Hydro.

Hodge is defending SB9 100m backstroke gold from Birmingham. (Reuters: Jeremy Lee)

Hodge's international journey began in Glasgow as a 14-year-old at the 2015 Para Swimming World Championships.

2026 marks his third Commonwealth Games, where he will try to defend the SB9 100m backstroke gold he won in Birmingham.

"I've been lucky enough to compete at two Commonwealth Games already, and I've watched the team come into the stadium both times and felt so much pride watching the green and gold walking in," Hodge said.

Australia's Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games baton. (Supplied: Commonwealth Games Australia)

"To now have that role myself, to have it happen in Glasgow of all places, the same city where I made my international debut, means the Games already feel special.

"It's the first time that I'll march too. I'm usually competing first day. I can't wait to feel the excitement."

The baton relay started at Buckingham Palace in March last year, when King Charles III put his full message into Scotland's baton.

Unlike previous years, every nation has their own, each containing one word of the message, which will be read in full by the King at the opening ceremony.

It is also the first time a King's baton has been carried for the Commonwealth Games, with the royal tradition starting at the 1958 Cardiff Games, five years after the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

World.title: French modelling scout with links to Epstein found dead, prosecutors say
World.content:
A French modelling scout with close ties to the late US financier Jeffrey Epstein has been found dead at his home outside Paris, prosecutors say.

Under investigation in France, Daniel Siad, 69, was one of several French men accused of aiding Epstein traffic and abuse women.

Mr Siad had not yet been questioned by investigators, but had denied the allegations, saying he wanted to be heard and give his version of events.

"An investigation to determine the cause of death was opened on Monday evening following the discovery," the prosecutor's office in the Paris suburb of Nanterre said.

An autopsy will be carried out as part of the probe.

His lawyer Menya Arab-Tigrine did not immediately respond when contacted by AFP.

French investigators had been investigating Mr Siad over allegations including for rape and human trafficking.

Daniel Siad was one of several French men accused of aiding Jeffrey Epstein traffic and abuse women. (AP: New York State Sex Offender Registry)

Mr Siad's name appeared in more than 1,000 documents released as part of the declassified Epstein files.

He likened his efforts to recruit women to fishing.

"In This busyness I feel like fisherman some time I cache quick, some time no fish," Siad wrote in English in an email to Epstein in 2014.

Mr Siad had insisted that the American convicted sex offender had "taken advantage of his trust".

French authorities in 2020 arrested modelling agent Jean-Luc Brunel after allegations he procured women for the US billionaire. He was found dead in prison in 2022.

Epstein died in prison in 2019 while awaiting trial for sex trafficking.

'Denied justice'

For victims, Mr Siad represented a possible avenue to finally "shed light on what happened" in relation to Epstein, said Juliette G., a former French model who says Siad recruited her in 2004 to introduce her to Epstein.

How Epstein targeted girls with dreams Admission into elite universities. A job that promised travel around the world. An audition for Victoria's Secret. This is how Jeffery Epstein lured his victims.

"Another link in the chain has disappeared that could have helped uncover the truth and identify those responsible," said the woman, who has asked to withhold her surname to protect her privacy.

Former Swedish model Ebba Karlsson, now in her fifties, filed the first complaint against Siad in February, accusing him of raping her when she was 20.

"It's very frustrating," Ms Karlsson told AFP.

"He was very close to be arrested. We worked so hard for this, trying to have justice."

She has also accused Mr Siad of introducing her to Gerald Marie, the former European head of the Elite modelling agency, whom she has also accused of rape.

Several women have accused Mr Marie of rape and human trafficking and urged France to investigate him for possible links to Epstein. He has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing.

Ex-BBC journalist Lisa Brinkworth, who co-founded a collective to support victims of model industry abuse, said she was shocked by the news of Mr Siad's death.

"It feels like victims are being denied justice," she added.

"It is appalling that he had not been detained."

ABC/AFP

World.title: China demands Australia stop 'inciting confrontation' over South China Sea
World.content:
China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has demanded Australia stop "exaggerating tensions and inciting confrontation" over the South China Sea after Penny Wong warned Beijing against "destabilising" conduct in the region.

The comments came after China and the Philippines blamed one another for a physical confrontation between the China Coast Guard and the Philippine Navy in the South China Sea on Monday.

On Wednesday Senator Wong said Australia was concerned about "aggression" and "destabilising conduct" and that countries had a "choice to make" about how to respond.

When asked about Senator Wong's comments, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said that "whenever there is the slightest disturbance at sea … the same small handful of countries rush to the forefront to oppose China without regard for the facts".

"China urges the relevant countries to stop exaggerating tensions and inciting confrontation, and to genuinely respect the efforts made by regional countries to maintain peace and stability in the South China Sea," Mr Lin said.

China says Australia is inciting confrontation amid tension over the launching of a missile that landed in the intended area. (CCTV)

The spat comes against the backdrop of an intense bout of regional diplomacy in the Philippines, which is hosting dozens of foreign ministers and senior officials for the annual ASEAN meeting in Manila.

The issue of China's behaviour loomed large ahead of the meeting, and ASEAN foreign ministers are eager to make progress on a South China Sea code of conduct that they hope will be finalised by the end of the year.

But the physical confrontation, in which a Filipino sailor was struck on the head with a baton, threw the issue back into the spotlight.

At a press conference, local journalists asked Senator Wong about the incident, as well as a Chinese missile test and rising tensions in the region.

"We are concerned about some of the aggression we are seeing, we are concerned about some of the destabilising conduct we are seeing," the foreign minister said.

"The countries of the region have a choice to make about how we all respond to that and Australia believes we should respond to that by working for peace and stability … [and] by continuing to call for and encouraging compliance with observation of international law and of safe and professional conduct at sea and in the air."

Senator Wong met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Tuesday night and raised Australia's concerns over China's missile test earlier this month.

China fired a dummy warhead from a nuclear-powered submarine. It landed in the Pacific, around the exclusive economic zone of Tuvalu.

Minister to use ASEAN as platform

The verbal stoush comes as the foreign minister prepares to deliver a sometimes-grim speech on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Thursday, where she will urge for freedom of navigation to be protected and warn the region that no "single power" should be able to "set the terms of our future".

Senator Wong is expected to use the address to make it clear that critical waterways like the Strait of Hormuz must remain toll-free.

"The Strait of Hormuz shows what we in this region have always understood … that people suffer when a strait is weaponised," she will say.

She will once again take aim at China over its recent ballistic missile test, saying it "came with too little information and notification, particularly to the Philippines — which the missile flew over — and Pacific nations, near where the missile landed".

"It comes in the context of China's rapid military build-up, including of its nuclear arsenal, without the transparency or reassurance the region expects," she will say.

"Which is why Australia has described the test as provocative and destabilising."

She is also set to urge other countries in the region to "resist the urge to turn inwards" and "the trend away from rules to use of power" in the face of global strategic ruptures and China's growing might.

"It demands we invest in our region, in our relationships, in the rules — in our collective resilience — before it is too late," she will warn.

"Before the rules are so diminished that they are no longer recognisable.

"Before crisis closes the door on cooperation."

While she does not mention the most recent South China Sea confrontation in her speech, she will also vow to continue "registering our concerns about China's vessels engaging in destabilising and dangerous conduct".

Philippines says navy personnel injured

China's Foreign Ministry has again blamed the Philippines for the physical altercation, in which the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said one of its navy personnel was injured.

Loading...

Footage of the incident shows the China Coast Guard and Philippine Navy briefly engaging each other from inflatable boats.

The incident took place at the Second Thomas Shoal, where the Philippines has a military outpost on a grounded ship.

"China has already made clear its solemn position regarding the malicious attacks by Philippine personnel against Chinese law enforcement officers," Mr Lin said.

For its part, AFP said China's Coast Guard "reacted violently and aggressively".

The Second Thomas Shoal is within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone, which China claims as its own, along with much of the South China Sea.

China's nine-dash line claim was rejected by a tribunal at The Hague a decade ago, but China disputes the ruling.

Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro raised the incident during talks with Mr Wang on Wednesday.

China reminds world of growing military power This latest military test demonstrates China's growing willingness to use its military strength to send a warning to the Pacific: that Beijing now has the military and nuclear means to assert its dominance in the region.

"I reiterated our strong protest over the unacceptable actions against Filipino personnel near Ayungin Shoal," Ms Lazaro said on social media.

The US State Department in a statement said it condemned "China's dangerous and aggressive actions against Philippine navy personnel".

"China's troubling pattern of provocation against lawful Philippine maritime operations undermines regional peace and stability and directly contradicts China's repeated commitments to resolve disputes peacefully," the statement said.

In a statement, the European Union delegation to the Philippines expressed "its deep concern over the steady increase of tensions and dangerous incidents in the South China Sea".

World.title: Government reveals proposed plans for new aquatic centre for 2032 Games
World.content:
The state government has unveiled fresh renders of the new National Aquatic Centre in Brisbane as it locks in a trio of architectural firms to design the marquee 2032 Olympics venue.

The Games Independent Infrastructure and Coordination Authority (GIICA) will take over Centenary Pool at Spring Hill on September 1, when early works will begin on site.

The state has chosen three firms to design the centre: ARM Architecture, NH Architecture and Queensland-based Arkhefield.

The proposed design features a wave-shaped roof.

The Centenary Pool at Spring Hill is set to close on August 31. (ABC News)

Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie will make the announcement tomorrow, six years out from the start of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Brisbane.

"This design trio will develop an iconic new home for high-performance aquatic athletes, as well as a legacy for community sport," Mr Bleijie said.

Five years since Brisbane secured the Olympics Broken promises and scarcely broken ground. Five years since Brisbane secured the 2032 Olympic Games, this is the state of play.

"This isn't just a venue for a few weeks in 2032.

"It's a lasting investment in Queensland's future that will support community sport, high-performance athletes and keeping us cool for generations to come."

NH Architecture played a role in the redevelopment of Melbourne Park, while ARM Architecture delivered the RAC Arena in Perth.

The centre is expected to have up to 25,000 seats during the Games, with a legacy capacity of 8,000 seats.

Mr Bleijie was asked today whether the capacity could be scaled back to save costs, but he did not directly answer the question.

He insisted, though, the $7.1 billion funding envelope for Games infrastructure would not change.

Kids lining up to leap off a high dive platform at Brisbane's Centenary Pool in 1966. (Supplied: Brisbane City Council)

"GIICA is leading the charge with respect to the delivery of those venues," Mr Bleijie said.

"What we said we were going to deliver was a National Aquatic Centre that will be the envy of the world.

"The best aquatic centre in the world at the moment is in Budapest, and they delivered an aquatic centre, and ours wants to be absolutely better than that."

Mr Bleijie also noted the government was going through a process with GIICA for all the venues.

"We did ask them to look at the costings, because when you appoint architects and designers, they have to do it within budget," the deputy premier added.

"Obviously GIICA has not released the results of the design phase and so forth … and we look forward to being briefed on that."

World.title: Details of allegations against Alan Jones emerge after judge decision
World.content:
Details of veteran broadcaster Alan Jones's alleged offending against six men can now be reported after a non-publication order was lifted by a judge.

Mr Jones, 85, is due to stand trial next month on 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching of six complainants, between 2003 and 2020.

He has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Some detail of the allegations, revealed in pre-trial hearings in the Downing Centre Local Court in Sydney, had been subject to interim non-publication orders sought by Mr Jones's defence team.

Lawyers for Mr Jones argued media coverage of the high-profile case could sway complainants and witnesses, and even the judge himself, just weeks before the trial.

But Judge Glenn Walsh on Wednesday dismissed a request for a formal suppression order over the crown case statement and other pre-trial argument, declaring because it was a judge-only trial, the risk of media reporting was lower.

"There is no jury panel to be prejudiced," Judge Walsh declared.

It means some details of Mr Jones's alleged offences against six men, who cannot be identified, can be revealed.

The evidence expected to be considered at trial was outlined by the prosecution during arguments about whether to admit tendency and coincidence evidence, which is evidence used to suggest a person has tendency to act on a particular state of mind.

Judge Walsh ruled on Monday that tendency and coincidence evidence could be admitted in the trial, meaning the prosecution can argue Mr Jones displayed a pattern of behaviour in his alleged offending.

Details of the allegations were heard in pre-trial hearings in the Downing Centre Local Court. (ABC News: Jak Rowland)

"I am not persuaded I will use the evidence in a prejudicial way," he told the court on Monday.

The court heard the prosecution will argue Mr Jones has a "sexual interest in men particularly younger than himself" and a "tendency to act upon that interest".

During argument about tendency evidence, prosecutors outlined details of allegations which can now be reported with the dismissal of an application for a non-publication order.

Jones's alleged acts of indecent assault

One man, Complainant C, made allegations that Mr Jones kissed and touched him several times, including in the lift at Mr Jones's Macquarie Street apartment.

The court heard the prosecution will allege Mr Jones put his hand over the man's crotch while he was driving Mr Jones, and then approached and kissed him in the lift.

Prosecutors allege the man told Mr Jones "no, no" and moved his head to the side, while on other occasions, he allegedly told Mr Jones he had a throat or mouth illness to stop a kiss.

On another occasion, the man is expected to allege he felt Mr Jones's hand on his upper thigh and crotch area at a lunch in Sydney.

Mr Jones faces eight charges in relation to Complainant C.

Another nine charges relate to another man, Complainant J, who the court heard was a young man when Mr Jones first met him.

Mr Jones allegedly gave him a mobile phone, and asked him to come visit him at his apartment.

During the young man's first visit to the apartment, Mr Jones allegedly put his arms around him, gave him a "squeeze" and a "peck" on the mouth, and told him, "I love you mate".

Mr Jones's alleged offences were against six younger men. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)

Other charges relate to incidents in the following year, where Mr Jones allegedly touched Complainant J's penis under his clothes while he was in a car with Mr Jones, driving to his second residence at Fitzroy Falls, in the NSW Southern Highlands.

It is alleged while at the house, Mr Jones committed other acts of indecent assault, including masturbating his own penis while touching the complainant and kissing him.

It is alleged Mr Jones kissed another man, Complainant I, on the corner of the mouth at a public event, and then texted him, saying something to the effect of "I want to be kissing you all night long".

That man further alleges that sometime between 2018 and 2020, he was in Mr Jones's home, when Mr Jones allegedly kissed him, pushing his genitalia into the complainant's body.

Complainant A is alleged to have been touched on the backside and kissed by Mr Jones at the broadcaster's Fitzroy Falls home.

Prosecutors will tell the court the man recalled being shocked by the alleged incident.

Another man, Complainant H, has alleged Mr Jones sexually touched him without consent on the backside and back at an event.

Non-publication order dismissed

Mr Jones's defence lawyers argued against the tendency evidence being admitted, saying it did not have significant probative value.

In deciding to dismiss the application for a non-publication order, Judge Walsh said he was not convinced reporting of pre-trial arguments would impede the course of justice.

"No material presented show that any media reporting to date has not been fair and accurate," he said.

The former 2GB and 2UE breakfast radio host is alleged to have committed the offences against the men during the time he worked in radio.

An investigation into the alleged offending, and his subsequent arrest in 2024, happened following a series of stories published in the Sydney Morning Herald, which made allegations against Mr Jones.

Mr Jones has always maintained his innocence.

He has not appeared in court for pre-trial hearings.

World.title: Doctor reveals injuries of woman allegedly sexually assaulted by Yung Filly
World.content:
WARNING: This story contains details some readers may find distressing, including descriptions of alleged sexual assault.

Graphic photographs of injuries allegedly inflicted by an internationally renowned YouTube star on an infatuated fan in his hotel room after a concert have been shown to a jury at his sexual assault trial in a Perth court.

Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, known to his millions of fans as Yung Filly, is on trial in the Perth District Court, accused of the brutal rape and assault of a 20-year-old woman at the Intercontinental Hotel in Perth's CBD in September 2024.

The 30-year-old rapper had been in Perth performing at Bar1, a waterfront venue in Perth's northern suburbs, and after the show had taken the young woman back to his hotel.

The pair had consensual sex in his room at the Intercontinental, before he allegedly violently raped her and repeatedly assaulted her, including biting and slapping her on the face, neck and breasts, strangling her, spitting in her mouth and forcing her to perform oral sex.

Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos's social media profiles have garnered millions of followers. (ABC News: David Weber)

Mr Barrientos denies all the charges against him, which include sexual penetration without consent, impeding a person's breathing and assault.

Today the court heard evidence from sexual assault specialist Geraldine Hoy, who examined the young woman at the Sexual Assault Resource Centre two days after her alleged ordeal.

Multiple bruises

Dr Hoy took a series of close-up photographs of the 20-year-old's face, neck and breasts that were shown to the jury, depicting multiple large bruises and swellings.

The 21 photos included what Dr Hoy described as a "green purply" bruise on her neck, a linear bruise on her neck and a "large … yellow bruise just above the right areola area of the breast".

Court hears Yung Filly choked, sexually assaulted young fan A Perth court hears disturbing details of the YouTube personality's alleged sexual assault of a young woman who had a "celebrity crush" on him.

Nearby on the same breast was another bruise measuring 4 centimetres x 8 centimetres, as well as a bruise that Dr Hoy described as yellow in colour.

Describing the photos in detail as they were displayed in court, Dr Hoy said the bruises on her face included two linear red swollen bruises on her right cheek, and bruising on the left side of her face that extended to her neck.

Dr Hoy said some of the bruising and swelling on the left side of the 20-year-old's neck could have been caused by obstructing the jugular vein, a form of strangulation.

Earlier the trial heard the 20-year-old woman had a "celebrity crush" on Mr Barrientos and had spoken of him as "her future husband".

She had worn her "lucky" white top to the gig in the hope of gaining access to the VIP area of the venue to get close to him, the court heard, which she was ultimately able to do late in the evening, before leaving with the rapper and his entourage in a van, back to his hotel.

The trial continues.

World.title: Jail for acccountant who gambled away $878,000 stolen from IGA
World.content:
An accountant for a network of IGA supermarkets in New South Wales has been jailed for defrauding $878,000.

Narelle Labuts, 61, worked with the Singh Group, which owns 10 IGA stores in the Hunter Valley.

She was sacked in 2021 after a bank flagged an unusual transaction.

Labuts stole the company's money by using white font on 522 transactions to hide her misconduct over a four-year period, the Newcastle District Court heard.

In October 2024, police charged her with obtaining financial advantage by deception and making a false document to obtain a financial advantage.

Labuts pleaded guilty at the end of last year.

Today she was sentenced to three and a half years in prison with a two-year non-parole period.

Judge Tim Gartelmann SC said what began as an opportunistic crime spiralled into something "that required significant planning and organising".

"The sentences for fraud offences must deter others to commit them," he said.

" They are easy to commit and hard to detect. "

Narelle Labuts was sacked after an irregular transaction was flagged. (Facebook)

The court heard Labuts had only returned a fraction of the stolen money, repaying $3,500 while the IGA network clawed back a further $9,000 by refusing to pay her entitlements.

At the sentencing hearing Labuts said she was addicted to gambling and that 90 per cent of the embezzled funds had gone into poker machines.

When the Crown asked her what happened to the remaining $80,000 that had not been gambled, she said "to be honest, I couldn't tell you".

Labuts said she knew that what she was doing was wrong thing but was "praying for a big win to return it all back".

"The house always wins, so it never eventuated," she said tearfully.

Labuts said she was "so incredibly sorry" and acknowledged she had "destroyed the trust [her employer] put in me".

Narelle Labuts said she gambled most of the money. (ABC Newcastle: Alex Turner-Cohen)

The court heard she has since worked as a bookkeeper at a transport and a concreting company, but did not disclose why her employment at the IGA network came to an abrupt end.

She said she would "probably" tell future employers about the conviction because it was now common knowledge.

Defence barrister Stephen Hopper emphasised that Labuts was addressing her gambling addiction and had been getting counselling since June 2022.

Labuts disagreed with a suggestion from the Crown that she only sought help for her gambling problem because she had been caught.

She will be eligible for parole in July 2028.

The airport Dusseldorf Airport (DUS) is the fourth-largest airport in Germany with 70 airlines flying to 177 destinations across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Dusseldorf Airport is Germany’s fourth busiest. The flight Qatar QR86 from Dusseldorf, Germany, to Doha, Qatar (DOH).



The arrival 



Despite my timely arrival, check-in is slow as there are family groups with loads of luggage in front of me. My bag is carry-on sized, but is too heavy and needs to be checked in, so although I feel silly waiting to hand it over, it being so small, I’m glad to be bag-free for my two-hour transit in Doha en route to Australia. Security Passing through security is straightforward and thorough and there’s no friendliness from the security staff who take their job (thankfully) super seriously. We’re all being processed on an assembly line; I’m just one of the 20 million people who pass through this major regional airport each year. Food and drink Marche, with its vegetarian options, is a welcome sight among airport dining.



I only have a six-hour flight ahead of me so I’d rather eat something good on the ground and skip the in-flight options. However, as a vegetarian I’m not optimistic. Even when I can find something without meat, it’s rarely very appetising. There are the usual kiosks and cafes, but I’m excited when I see a Marche restaurant, which has an on-site bakery and pizza, pasta and schnitzel kitchen. I make a bee-line for “vegetarian island”, a stand-alone cabinet with excellent vegetarian and vegan food ranging from salads to hot dishes including a tempting potato gratin. After two weeks in a wurst wonderland, this is exactly the kind of food I want to eat. According to Clean Energy Wire, about 10 per cent of Germans are vegetarian or vegan, another 40 per cent only consume meat occasionally and both groups skew younger, so this offering makes sense. Judging by the amount of people queueing to order, it’s the most popular place to eat. I pick up a small plate of salads and a green juice and head to the timber tables to enjoy the sunshine streaming in from the floor-to-ceiling windows. Retail therapy I spot FC Bayern Munich merchandise, mini cuckoo clocks, souvenirs of the city’s iconic Radschlager (cartwheeler) sculptures, steins and Altbier liqueur, a specialty liquor found in Dusseldorf. There’s a luxury boutique of knits, lingerie and socks from German brand Falke, books and newspapers in multiple languages, and the usual tech, games and travel supplies. Passing time



A bar in the middle of the gate lounges has expansive views of the runway, so it’s hard not to want to pull up a stool and make the most of the opportunity to have one more taste of Germany. Many of my fellow passengers do the same. Lounge chairs at the gate can’t compete with a comfy bar stool, even if I am only having a lemonade. Related Article ★★★★

World.title: Third time’s a charm: Kennedy and Hodge named as Australia’s flag and baton bearers
World.content:
Breaking SportCommonwealth Games Third time’s a charm: Kennedy and Hodge named as Australia’s flag and baton bearers Billie Eder July 22, 2026 — 11:59pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Commonwealth Games champions Nina Kennedy and Tim Hodge have been named the Australian flag and baton bearers for the opening ceremony in Glasgow. Kennedy and Hodge, both reigning champions from Birmingham 2022, will lead the Australian team out on Friday July 24 (AEST). Competing at their third Commonwealth Games, Kennedy and Hodge were announced as the flag and baton bearers by Australian Chef de Mission Petria Thomas at the Bridge Gardens in Glasgow, just up from the city’s River Clyde, on Wednesday afternoon (local time). Commonwealth Games and Olympic champions Nina Kennedy and Timothy Hodge. AP/Getty Kennedy, the Olympic and Commonwealth Games pole vault champion, has struggled with injury since Paris 2024 to be in Glasgow, and said it meant more than she could put into words to lead the team out at the opening ceremony.



“I am so proud to follow in the footsteps of so many great Australians who have carried the flag before me,” Kennedy said. “The Commonwealth Games have always meant so much to me; it’s where I won my first medal back in 2018. “This is my third Games, and I’m lucky enough to be defending my title. My final isn’t until later in the week, so I’ll get a bit of a sleep-in the morning after. I’ve worked with our team to make sure I’m as prepared as I can be, and there’s no version of the Games where I’d miss the chance to carry that flag.” Nina Kennedy after winning pole vault gold in Birmingham 2022. Getty Hodge, who will be defending his title in the men’s 100m backstroke S9, was honoured to be given the role.



Related Article Commonwealth Games The defector, the bodybuilder and the actor: The Games moments you must not miss “I’ve been lucky enough to compete at two Commonwealth Games already, and I’ve watched the team come into the stadium both times and felt so much pride watching the green and gold walking in,” Hodge said “To now have that role myself, to have it happen in Glasgow of all places, the same city where I made my international debut, means the Games already feel special. “It’s the first time that I’ll march too, I’m usually competing first day. I can’t wait to feel the excitement.” Timothy Hodge after breaking the individual medley world record. Getty Images



Thomas said Kennedy and Hodge were given the honour not just because of their results, but because of their leadership in the Australian team. Related Article Commonwealth Games Ridge found love on reality TV, but it almost cost him a spot at the Commonwealth Games “Each of them has longevity, character and humility, and the support of the whole Australian sporting community behind them,” Thomas said. “Nina gives just as much off the track as she does on, and we know she is a proven performer ... Tim is at his third Commonwealth Games, with two Paralympic gold medals and a world record to his name. “He made his Australian debut in this very city over a decade ago, and everywhere he goes he brings a calm yet inspiring approach that lifts those around him.



“I know they’ll lead our team out with pride and grace.” Follow our coverage of the Commonwealth Games with live blogs covering every moment of the action from 6pm AEST daily, beginning Friday, July 24. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport are sent every Monday.

World.title: Pain had Torrie Lewis in tears just warming up. But weeks later, she smashed a national record
World.content:
Just weeks ago, Torrie Lewis sat on the track and cried. It was only the warm-up for training, and she couldn’t even get through that without pain knifing up her leg. If it were not for the Commonwealth Games coming up, she would have put a line through her season. Australian sprinter Torrie Lewis has again broken her own national record. Getty Images The same Achilles that had torn last year and cruelled her season was screaming at her again. She hadn’t torn it again, but it was not right. The injury forced her to pull out of what would have been her last competition before the Commonwealth Games, where the athletics program begins next Monday. With her Achilles the way it was, she doubted she could run the sprint double and the sprint relay. So she went to Slovakia for the PTS meet in Banska Bystrica not knowing what would happen.



She was there for clarity – she told this masthead in a pre-Games interview that what happened in Slovakia would be the decider for her schedule in Glasgow. She will now certainly run the sprint double at the Commonwealth Games, after breaking the national record, her own national 100-metre record and nearly becoming the first Australian woman to break 11 seconds. Loading She also beat a five-time Olympic champion in the process, won the 200m and, most importantly, was pain free when she ran – and woke up with her Achilles feeling good. “I just saw it was a strong field with Elaine Thompson [Herah from Jamaica, a five-time Olympic champion] and just wanted to try and win it. I wasn’t thinking of a record at all but am thrilled that I ran well and broke it,” said Lewis, who ran 11.04 seconds. She won her 200m in 22.66s.



“I was just really happy, I’ve been watching her [Thompson-Herah] for so many years winning at the Olympics and of course I know she is not in her peak shape, but it’s pretty cool to beat someone of that calibre. And I was very happy to have a hug with her at the end. Related Article Updated

World athletics championships Eight-centimetre hamstring tear ends Gout Gout’s under-20 world title tilt “I feel like I could run again today. So that does help my confidence going into Glasgow, knowing how busy the schedule is.” For perspective, Lewis broke the national record when in normal circumstances she would not be running. “[Slovakia] was the last part of the plan my coach wanted me to do,” she said in the interview before the meet.



“I am a little bit unsure. Normally six days out from a competition I would not want to compete, but I am really unsure where I am at. “Last year I tore my Achilles and I missed a lot of competitions, a lot of training, but I came back and literally the first outdoor competition in China it started hurting again. I was worried. It’s the same one. “You would say that I couldn’t expect much of myself given the impact on training, but my last race in Scotland I ran my second-fastest time .06 outside my PB, so that’s why I wanted to do this competition in Slovakia and see if I can keep momentum. “I still have good hopes of what I can do. It [Scotland] surprised me, but I have been so determined all year to run well in Glasgow, even if I am in pain. “The pain has gotten better this last week and a half, but a couple of weeks ago it was so bad I was crying just warming up. If I was not so determined to run at the Comm Games I would have pulled the plug on the season and started again for sure.



“I really want to go to Glasgow. I have spoken to the physios from Australia and the Netherlands and had scans, and they think running on it won’t make it worse, it will just be painful. It’s not at risk of tearing again. It didn’t need surgery last time and I don’t think it will this time. “My results won’t change a lot between [Slovakia] and Glasgow, you cannot improve a lot in a week and a half, but hopefully at a major championship I am able to run a bit better.” Queenslander Lewis first broke the national record as a 19-year-old in Canberra in 2024 when she ran 11.10 seconds, beating Melissa Breen’s record from 2014 of 11.11s. Lewis lowered that time again during heats at last year’s world athletics championships with a run of 11.08. Related Article Commonwealth Games The 75-year-old great-grandmother making her Commonwealth Games debut This latest record comes just months after Lewis was retrospectively awarded the gold medal in March for the 200m at the 2024 under-20 world championships after winner Adaejah Hodge had tested positive for a banned metabolic modulator.



Hodge, who competes for the Virgin Islands, received a heavy discount to her ban, which will allow her to compete in Glasgow, setting up a showdown with Lewis as Hodge has been named to race in the 100m and 200m. Lewis is scheduled to run in the 100m, 200m and 4x100m relay in Glasgow after being named in the 55-member Australian team along with fellow rising sprint stars Lachlan Kennedy (100m, 200m and 4x100m relay) and Eddie Nketia (100m). The competition is a valuable international building block on the path to the LA 2028 Olympic Games. Young sensation Gout Gout will not compete in Glasgow, having planned to run at this year’s world under-20 championships instead, but that was shelved after he suffered a serious hamstring injury in training. He is expected to be out of competition until next year. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport are sent every Monday.

World.title: We feel your pain: PM sets election battle lines with One Nation, pledges cost of living relief
World.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will set up his bid for a third term with a promise of further expensive cost of living measures to address financial stress fuelling One Nation’s ascension as he expands a program to pay health workers as they study. However, Labor ministers are downplaying the prospect of a tax on gas exports before a fight at its national conference on the popular proposal, signifying tension in Labor ranks over how aggressively Albanese is pursuing populist causes. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addresses the national Labor conference in 2023. Alex Ellinghausen In a speech to Labor faithful on Thursday that Albanese will use to frame the election’s battle lines, the prime minister will invoke 135 years of Labor tradition on practical responses to boost workers’ living standards rather than “raging against a system … without a plan to fix it”. Albanese will say that “people have been given every reason to feel like the economy is simply not working for them” as he seeks to boost the government’s political fortunes and meet pessimistic voters where they are.



“That goes deeper than sentiment – it’s a reality people are up against,” he will say, according to an advance copy of his speech, noting he was riding “rough seas” after a series of economic shocks and an oil crisis sparked by the Middle East war. Related Article Political leadership Albanese once took on his own frontbench. Now he’s in charge, that would never happen “It’s how we prove that the status quo is not set in stone. How we demonstrate to Australians that their hard work will pay off, that their effort is worth it. That faults in the system can be fixed [and] that Labor is delivering the real change Australians deserve.” His emphasis on helping voters pay their bills, and stating this was a fundamental contrast with his opponents, suggests that Labor will test the fiscal boundaries and focus on cost of living relief in its next two pre-election budgets after spending political capital on revenue-raising tax concession changes this year. Albanese does not mention One Nation by name but his exhortations to reject populist politics underline the upended political dynamic two years out from the next election. Just over a year after his historic win, Albanese’s party has dropped 6.5 percentage points on first-preference vote, according to Poll Bludger’s average of major polls, and is only narrowly ahead of Pauline Hanson’s party, with the Coalition languishing in third.



Albanese will take a veiled swipe at Hanson’s recent controversies on race relations by suggesting the surging populist leader was “blaming people who cannot defend themselves” and championing a form of politics that “doesn’t build anything”. In the face of criticism from Opposition Leader Angus Taylor about an expanding and unproductive care sector, Albanese will on Thursday announce Labor is extending financial support to health students while they undertake training as part of their degrees. Labor did not provide the cost of the policy. Related Article University University in 2027: see how much your degree will cost This will offer a weekly stipend to thousands of students in physio and occupational therapy, clinical psychology, pharmacy and podiatry, speech pathology, audiology, radiography, rehab therapies and paramedics. The government first announced in its 2024 budget that it would give weekly payments to students undertaking practical placements for their teaching, nursing, midwifery and social work qualifications – one of its cost of living pitches to young Australians before the 2025 election. The indexed subsidy is almost $340 a week.



But allied health groups and young students in health professions wanted the prac payments extended to them. The issue has been taken up in parliament by independents Helen Haines and David Pocock. Photo: Matt Golding Parliamentary Budget Office modelling commissioned by Haines found that extending the payments to health and medical students – including psychologists, paramedics and physiotherapists – would cost $290.4 million through to the 2028-29 financial year, on top of $505.3 million budgeted for the current scheme over the same period. Albanese said the program had changed the lives of students who were struggling to make ends meet during university, moving in with their parents or juggling part-time work with their placements to pay rent. Causing headaches for Albanese has been a campaign from MPs including Labor’s Ed Husic, unions, the left-wing Australia Institute think tank, and online content creators to levy gas firms with a 25 per cent export tax.



The issue caught on in the public discourse right at the same time as Albanese was trying to secure fuel from Asian neighbours at the start of the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Many Asian nations that supply fuel rely on Australia’s gas exports, so Albanese scuppered the idea. Related Article Analysis

ALP Flying the flag for a fight nobody else wanted to have However, a section of the party’s draft platform states that Labor will ensure Australians “receive a fairer return from their natural resources”, opening the door to a tax later this term. Treasurer Jim Chalmers and others in the government have been open to a fresh revenue grab on resources firms. The renewed fighting in the Middle East means that the issue of fuel scarcity may again come to the fore, adding pressure on Albanese to downplay a new tax as he did on the weekend. Ministers have also tried to quash talk of a tax. “The position of the government has been that we haven’t supported a gas tax,” Environment Minister Murray Watt said on Nine’s Today program on Wednesday.



“Our focus has been making sure that we can get the fuel and gas supplies that we need into the country, and also to do what we can to keep gas prices low.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: Appetite for reflection
World.content:
Paul Taylor of Winston Hills doesn’t mind a bit of mobile fare when he says: “I’ve only just noticed that the badge on newer models of BYD appears as CYE when the car approaches in the rear-view mirror. I did wonder about any subliminal messaging but can only conclude that it may be a traditionally formatted attempt to cash in on the burgeoning fast food delivery car market. Perhaps it should be read as Express Yum Cha.”

“I can sympathise with Jack Dikian’s childhood recollections of watching Play School (C8) and his disappointment in choosing the incorrect window,” says Viv Munter of Tumbi Umbi. “During the ’70s, I recall watching Romper Room and waiting with bated breath for Miss Helena to acknowledge my name when she peered through the magic mirror. Disappointingly, she could never see me.”

“Hey, Jim Dewar. As one of your old fossils (C8), I’m sure that there must be someone, somewhere, that would complain about my demise,” hopes Robert Hosking of Paddington. “Meanwhile, I am seeking bids from cashed-up billionaires for the calcium components of my remains. Do I hear a starting bid of $1m?”

Jennifer Killen of St Peters has another regional first-time film (C8) experience: “My first visit to Leeton’s beautiful Roxy Theatre was a big adventure for a preschooler. I remember nothing of the movie which engrossed my mother and great-aunt, but the decades have not erased the memory of climbing up and over the seats behind, all the way until I reached the top. I then realised I could open the blinds and look out across the main street from above. Much more fun than watching the movie.”

“In the early ’50s, my parents, my brother and I went to the pictures every Saturday night in Marrickville,” recalls Dennis Fardy of Warriewood. “We had reserved seats and wore pyjamas and dressing gowns so we could go straight to bed on getting home. Ironically, the only movie I can remember from that time is The Robe.”

I’ve worked with our team to make sure I’m as prepared as I can be, and there’s no version of the Games where I’d miss the chance to carry that flag.” Nina Kennedy after winning pole vault gold in Birmingham 2022. Getty Hodge, who will be defending his title in the men’s 100m backstroke S9, was honoured to be given the role.



Related Article Commonwealth Games The defector, the bodybuilder and the actor: The Games moments you must not miss “I’ve been lucky enough to compete at two Commonwealth Games already, and I’ve watched the team come into the stadium both times and felt so much pride watching the green and gold walking in,” Hodge said “To now have that role myself, to have it happen in Glasgow of all places, the same city where I made my international debut, means the Games already feel special. “It’s the first time that I’ll march too, I’m usually competing first day. I can’t wait to feel the excitement.” Timothy Hodge after breaking the individual medley world record. Getty Images



Thomas said Kennedy and Hodge were given the honour not just because of their results, but because of their leadership in the Australian team. Related Article Commonwealth Games Ridge found love on reality TV, but it almost cost him a spot at the Commonwealth Games “Each of them has longevity, character and humility, and the support of the whole Australian sporting community behind them,” Thomas said. “Nina gives just as much off the track as she does on, and we know she is a proven performer ... Tim is at his third Commonwealth Games, with two Paralympic gold medals and a world record to his name. “He made his Australian debut in this very city over a decade ago, and everywhere he goes he brings a calm yet inspiring approach that lifts those around him.



“I know they’ll lead our team out with pride and grace.” Follow our coverage of the Commonwealth Games with live blogs covering every moment of the action from 6pm AEST daily, beginning Friday, July 24. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport are sent every Monday.

World.title: Pain had Torrie Lewis in tears just warming up. But weeks later, she smashed a national record
World.content:
Just weeks ago, Torrie Lewis sat on the track and cried. It was only the warm-up for training, and she couldn’t even get through that without pain knifing up her leg. If it were not for the Commonwealth Games coming up, she would have put a line through her season. Australian sprinter Torrie Lewis has again broken her own national record. Getty Images The same Achilles that had torn last year and cruelled her season was screaming at her again. She hadn’t torn it again, but it was not right. The injury forced her to pull out of what would have been her last competition before the Commonwealth Games, where the athletics program begins next Monday. With her Achilles the way it was, she doubted she could run the sprint double and the sprint relay. So she went to Slovakia for the PTS meet in Banska Bystrica not knowing what would happen.



She was there for clarity – she told this masthead in a pre-Games interview that what happened in Slovakia would be the decider for her schedule in Glasgow. She will now certainly run the sprint double at the Commonwealth Games, after breaking the national record, her own national 100-metre record and nearly becoming the first Australian woman to break 11 seconds. Loading She also beat a five-time Olympic champion in the process, won the 200m and, most importantly, was pain free when she ran – and woke up with her Achilles feeling good. “I just saw it was a strong field with Elaine Thompson [Herah from Jamaica, a five-time Olympic champion] and just wanted to try and win it. I wasn’t thinking of a record at all but am thrilled that I ran well and broke it,” said Lewis, who ran 11.04 seconds. She won her 200m in 22.66s.



“I was just really happy, I’ve been watching her [Thompson-Herah] for so many years winning at the Olympics and of course I know she is not in her peak shape, but it’s pretty cool to beat someone of that calibre. And I was very happy to have a hug with her at the end. Related Article Updated

World athletics championships Eight-centimetre hamstring tear ends Gout Gout’s under-20 world title tilt “I feel like I could run again today. So that does help my confidence going into Glasgow, knowing how busy the schedule is.” For perspective, Lewis broke the national record when in normal circumstances she would not be running. “[Slovakia] was the last part of the plan my coach wanted me to do,” she said in the interview before the meet.



“I am a little bit unsure. Normally six days out from a competition I would not want to compete, but I am really unsure where I am at. “Last year I tore my Achilles and I missed a lot of competitions, a lot of training, but I came back and literally the first outdoor competition in China it started hurting again. I was worried. It’s the same one. “You would say that I couldn’t expect much of myself given the impact on training, but my last race in Scotland I ran my second-fastest time .06 outside my PB, so that’s why I wanted to do this competition in Slovakia and see if I can keep momentum. “I still have good hopes of what I can do. It [Scotland] surprised me, but I have been so determined all year to run well in Glasgow, even if I am in pain. “The pain has gotten better this last week and a half, but a couple of weeks ago it was so bad I was crying just warming up. If I was not so determined to run at the Comm Games I would have pulled the plug on the season and started again for sure.



“I really want to go to Glasgow. I have spoken to the physios from Australia and the Netherlands and had scans, and they think running on it won’t make it worse, it will just be painful. It’s not at risk of tearing again. It didn’t need surgery last time and I don’t think it will this time. “My results won’t change a lot between [Slovakia] and Glasgow, you cannot improve a lot in a week and a half, but hopefully at a major championship I am able to run a bit better.” Queenslander Lewis first broke the national record as a 19-year-old in Canberra in 2024 when she ran 11.10 seconds, beating Melissa Breen’s record from 2014 of 11.11s. Lewis lowered that time again during heats at last year’s world athletics championships with a run of 11.08. Related Article Commonwealth Games The 75-year-old great-grandmother making her Commonwealth Games debut This latest record comes just months after Lewis was retrospectively awarded the gold medal in March for the 200m at the 2024 under-20 world championships after winner Adaejah Hodge had tested positive for a banned metabolic modulator.



Hodge, who competes for the Virgin Islands, received a heavy discount to her ban, which will allow her to compete in Glasgow, setting up a showdown with Lewis as Hodge has been named to race in the 100m and 200m. Lewis is scheduled to run in the 100m, 200m and 4x100m relay in Glasgow after being named in the 55-member Australian team along with fellow rising sprint stars Lachlan Kennedy (100m, 200m and 4x100m relay) and Eddie Nketia (100m). The competition is a valuable international building block on the path to the LA 2028 Olympic Games. Young sensation Gout Gout will not compete in Glasgow, having planned to run at this year’s world under-20 championships instead, but that was shelved after he suffered a serious hamstring injury in training. He is expected to be out of competition until next year. News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport are sent every Monday.

World.title: We feel your pain: PM sets election battle lines with One Nation, pledges cost of living relief
World.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will set up his bid for a third term with a promise of further expensive cost of living measures to address financial stress fuelling One Nation’s ascension as he expands a program to pay health workers as they study. However, Labor ministers are downplaying the prospect of a tax on gas exports before a fight at its national conference on the popular proposal, signifying tension in Labor ranks over how aggressively Albanese is pursuing populist causes. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese addresses the national Labor conference in 2023. Alex Ellinghausen In a speech to Labor faithful on Thursday that Albanese will use to frame the election’s battle lines, the prime minister will invoke 135 years of Labor tradition on practical responses to boost workers’ living standards rather than “raging against a system … without a plan to fix it”. Albanese will say that “people have been given every reason to feel like the economy is simply not working for them” as he seeks to boost the government’s political fortunes and meet pessimistic voters where they are.



“That goes deeper than sentiment – it’s a reality people are up against,” he will say, according to an advance copy of his speech, noting he was riding “rough seas” after a series of economic shocks and an oil crisis sparked by the Middle East war. Related Article Political leadership Albanese once took on his own frontbench. Now he’s in charge, that would never happen “It’s how we prove that the status quo is not set in stone. How we demonstrate to Australians that their hard work will pay off, that their effort is worth it. That faults in the system can be fixed [and] that Labor is delivering the real change Australians deserve.” His emphasis on helping voters pay their bills, and stating this was a fundamental contrast with his opponents, suggests that Labor will test the fiscal boundaries and focus on cost of living relief in its next two pre-election budgets after spending political capital on revenue-raising tax concession changes this year. Albanese does not mention One Nation by name but his exhortations to reject populist politics underline the upended political dynamic two years out from the next election. Just over a year after his historic win, Albanese’s party has dropped 6.5 percentage points on first-preference vote, according to Poll Bludger’s average of major polls, and is only narrowly ahead of Pauline Hanson’s party, with the Coalition languishing in third.



Albanese will take a veiled swipe at Hanson’s recent controversies on race relations by suggesting the surging populist leader was “blaming people who cannot defend themselves” and championing a form of politics that “doesn’t build anything”. In the face of criticism from Opposition Leader Angus Taylor about an expanding and unproductive care sector, Albanese will on Thursday announce Labor is extending financial support to health students while they undertake training as part of their degrees. Labor did not provide the cost of the policy. Related Article University University in 2027: see how much your degree will cost This will offer a weekly stipend to thousands of students in physio and occupational therapy, clinical psychology, pharmacy and podiatry, speech pathology, audiology, radiography, rehab therapies and paramedics. The government first announced in its 2024 budget that it would give weekly payments to students undertaking practical placements for their teaching, nursing, midwifery and social work qualifications – one of its cost of living pitches to young Australians before the 2025 election. The indexed subsidy is almost $340 a week.



But allied health groups and young students in health professions wanted the prac payments extended to them. The issue has been taken up in parliament by independents Helen Haines and David Pocock. Photo: Matt Golding Parliamentary Budget Office modelling commissioned by Haines found that extending the payments to health and medical students – including psychologists, paramedics and physiotherapists – would cost $290.4 million through to the 2028-29 financial year, on top of $505.3 million budgeted for the current scheme over the same period. Albanese said the program had changed the lives of students who were struggling to make ends meet during university, moving in with their parents or juggling part-time work with their placements to pay rent. Causing headaches for Albanese has been a campaign from MPs including Labor’s Ed Husic, unions, the left-wing Australia Institute think tank, and online content creators to levy gas firms with a 25 per cent export tax.



The issue caught on in the public discourse right at the same time as Albanese was trying to secure fuel from Asian neighbours at the start of the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Many Asian nations that supply fuel rely on Australia’s gas exports, so Albanese scuppered the idea. Related Article Analysis

ALP Flying the flag for a fight nobody else wanted to have However, a section of the party’s draft platform states that Labor will ensure Australians “receive a fairer return from their natural resources”, opening the door to a tax later this term. Treasurer Jim Chalmers and others in the government have been open to a fresh revenue grab on resources firms. The renewed fighting in the Middle East means that the issue of fuel scarcity may again come to the fore, adding pressure on Albanese to downplay a new tax as he did on the weekend. Ministers have also tried to quash talk of a tax. “The position of the government has been that we haven’t supported a gas tax,” Environment Minister Murray Watt said on Nine’s Today program on Wednesday.



“Our focus has been making sure that we can get the fuel and gas supplies that we need into the country, and also to do what we can to keep gas prices low.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. Subscribers can sign up to our weekly Inside Politics newsletter.

World.title: Appetite for reflection
World.content:
Paul Taylor of Winston Hills doesn’t mind a bit of mobile fare when he says: “I’ve only just noticed that the badge on newer models of BYD appears as CYE when the car approaches in the rear-view mirror. I did wonder about any subliminal messaging but can only conclude that it may be a traditionally formatted attempt to cash in on the burgeoning fast food delivery car market. Perhaps it should be read as Express Yum Cha.”

“I can sympathise with Jack Dikian’s childhood recollections of watching Play School (C8) and his disappointment in choosing the incorrect window,” says Viv Munter of Tumbi Umbi. “During the ’70s, I recall watching Romper Room and waiting with bated breath for Miss Helena to acknowledge my name when she peered through the magic mirror. Disappointingly, she could never see me.”

“Hey, Jim Dewar. As one of your old fossils (C8), I’m sure that there must be someone, somewhere, that would complain about my demise,” hopes Robert Hosking of Paddington. “Meanwhile, I am seeking bids from cashed-up billionaires for the calcium components of my remains. Do I hear a starting bid of $1m?”

Jennifer Killen of St Peters has another regional first-time film (C8) experience: “My first visit to Leeton’s beautiful Roxy Theatre was a big adventure for a preschooler. I remember nothing of the movie which engrossed my mother and great-aunt, but the decades have not erased the memory of climbing up and over the seats behind, all the way until I reached the top. I then realised I could open the blinds and look out across the main street from above. Much more fun than watching the movie.”

“In the early ’50s, my parents, my brother and I went to the pictures every Saturday night in Marrickville,” recalls Dennis Fardy of Warriewood. “We had reserved seats and wore pyjamas and dressing gowns so we could go straight to bed on getting home. Ironically, the only movie I can remember from that time is The Robe.”
